sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 82. Security, integration and scheduling (1.61.0)
sections.text: Version 1.60.0 (succession planning, 9-box, learning paths) is planned but not released yet; 1.61.0 follows 1.59.0.

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 82. Security, integration and scheduling (1.61.0) › 82.1 Networks allowed (IP allow-list)
sections.text:
- Settings › Sign-in security › **Networks allowed**: the IP addresses / networks (one per line, CIDR such as `94.200.10.0/24`, `#` starts a note) from which the company may be used, for **staff users** (employees in self service may sign in from anywhere) or **everybody**.
- Every company request from another network is refused (403, with the address ZEO saw). A sign-in is refused only when **every** company of the user refuses the network (a user of two companies can still reach the other one); the refused sign-in is written as an alert.
- Safety: a list that does not contain the address of the administrator saving it is refused; the server owner (Django superuser) is never refused.
- The address: the last X-Forwarded-For entry (the one the proxy added), else the connection address. Before 1.61.0 the first entry was used for the sign-in log and the API key IP check – a visitor could type it; now it cannot be faked. The proxy in front of ZEO must add the address (nginx: `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;`).

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 82. Security, integration and scheduling (1.61.0) › 82.2 Sign-in alerts
sections.text:
- A row in My sign-in › **Sign-in alerts** and an e-mail to the user when the account is signed in to from a **new network and a new device** (both not seen in the last 180 days; not on the first sign-in; at most one alert per address a day), when **wrong passwords lock** the account, and when a sign-in is **refused** because of the networks.
- The user answers **This was me** or **This was not me** – "not me" ends every sign-in of the user (also the current one) and asks for a new password at the next sign-in.
- Settings › Sign-in security: switch each e-mail on / off, and the alerts of the company's users of the last 90 days with their answer.
- Not testable here: the country of an address – it needs an outside IP database (a paid service); the alert shows the address.

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 82. Security, integration and scheduling (1.61.0) › 82.3 API v1
sections.text:
- `/api/v1/` – a small, stable API for integrations: employees, branches / departments / designations, leave requests and balances, attendance days, **attendance punches** (POST, for time clocks; the same punch twice is not added twice) and payslip totals. Field names do not change within v1; lists are paged (`page`, `page_size` ≤ 500); dates `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- API keys (Settings › API keys and webhooks) get **scopes** (employees:read, org:read, leave:read, attendance:read, attendance:write, payroll:read) and **API v1 only** (the key cannot call ZEO's internal addresses). A read-only key cannot have a write scope. The key acts as its user: that user's branches, and the user must have the rights to see the data; a key of a self-service employee is refused.
- Keys made before 1.61.0 keep working as before on the internal addresses; they need scopes to use `/api/v1/`.
- The page shows the endpoints, the filters and a `curl` example.

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 82. Security, integration and scheduling (1.61.0) › 82.4 Legal hold
sections.text:
- Settings › Data retention and privacy › **Legal holds**: place a hold on an employee (reason, case / claim number) and release it with a reason; released holds stay as history.
- While a hold is active ZEO refuses to delete the employee's records – the employee, documents and their fields, family and dependants, identity, letters, HR tickets, disciplinary cases, resignation, leave requests and payslips – from any screen, import undo or script, and refuses to anonymise them; the retention list leaves them out.

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 82. Security, integration and scheduling (1.61.0) › 82.5 Letter template versions
sections.text:
- Self service › Settings › Letter templates: every saved wording is a **version** (with *what changed*); **Versions** lists them with the date, who saved it and how many letters were issued with each; **Text** shows the old wording; **Restore** makes an old wording current again (as a new version).
- An issued letter records the template and the version it was issued with (its text was already kept).

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 82. Security, integration and scheduling (1.61.0) › 82.6 HR tickets: suggested category and priority
sections.text:
- A new HR ticket (self service, kiosk or entered by HR) gets a **suggested category and priority** with *how sure* and *why*: by the built-in rules (the category's **keywords**, any language; default keywords for the standard categories in English and Arabic; urgency words for the priority), or by the external AI when the server and the company switched it on and **HR tickets** is on in Settings › AI settings (subject and question are sent, not the employee's name; any failure falls back to the built-in rules).
- HR operations setup › *Ticket category and priority*: off / **suggest only** (default) / suggest and apply when at least N % sure. "Apply" moves a ticket from a **general category** (Other) to the suggested one – never out of a category the employee chose – and raises (never lowers) the priority. With suggestions on, an employee who does not choose a category gets the general one and the suggestion sorts it.
- On the ticket: **Use the suggestion** and **Suggest category** (read it again).

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 82. Security, integration and scheduling (1.61.0) › 82.7 Insurer member file
sections.text:
- People › **Insurer member file**: for a medical plan, the members on a date – each employee (principal) and their insured family members – with member type, relation, name (and Arabic name), gender, date of birth, age, marital status, nationality, Emirates ID, passport, visa / UID and file no., mobile, e-mail, work location, category, **salary band** (up to 4,000 / 4,001–12,000 / above 12,000 a month), member no., policy no., effective and end dates; or only the **changes since** a date (additions and deletions) for the monthly endorsement. Excel or CSV; members with missing data are listed.
- Family members: Employee › Family where *insured* is ticked (with gender, nationality, Emirates ID, passport, visa), else the dependants written on the enrolment.
- Insurers' templates differ: check the columns against your insurer's file before the first upload.

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 82. Security, integration and scheduling (1.61.0) › 82.8 Split shifts
sections.text:
- Shift planner › Shift master: **parts of the day** (2–4, e.g. 07:00–11:00 and 16:00–20:00, at least 15 minutes apart); the shift runs from the first part to the last; the time between the parts is unpaid and not in the hours.
- Attendance: coming back late after the gap is late, leaving before the gap is early; time present between the parts is not working time; a part not worked at all is flagged; overtime counts from the hours of the parts.

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 82. Security, integration and scheduling (1.61.0) › 82.9 Skills-based scheduling
sections.text:
- Shift master › **Skills needed**: skills from Learning › Skills with the level (1–5) and how many people, e.g. one person with *Basic life support* level 3 on the night shift.
- Roster › **Skills cover**: every day and shift where the people planned do not have the skills (people on leave do not count), and **Who can cover**: employees of the roster with the skill at the level who are not on leave – not planned or on a day off first, then by level – with **Put on the shift** (the usual rest-hour and week-hour checks run).

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 82. Security, integration and scheduling (1.61.0) › 82.10 Backup command
sections.text:
- `python manage.py zeo_backup` – a folder `backup-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS` with each PostgreSQL database (`pg_dump` custom format; the own databases of ZEO Cloud too), the uploaded files (`media.tar.gz`) and `manifest.json` (version, sizes, SHA-256); the new backup is checked (checksums, the archive can be read) and `last-backup.json` is written (System health › Last backup). Options: `--dir`, `--schema` (one company, no files), `--no-media`, `--keep N` (days; backups older than that made by this command are deleted, default 14), `--check <folder>`.
- Schedule it nightly and copy the folder off the server. Restore is done by hand on purpose: stop gunicorn and Celery, `createdb` a new database, `pg_restore --no-owner -d <new> db-default.dump`, point `.env` to it, `tar xzf media.tar.gz`, start again.

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 82. Security, integration and scheduling (1.61.0) › 82.11 Migration fix
sections.text: - `ZeoProperty/migrations/0003_complete_property_management.py` and `ZeoHR/migrations/0003_assignments_matrix.py` referred to core-app migrations that are not shipped (made only on our test server). On a server that keeps its own core-app migrations `migrate_schemas` stopped with *"dependencies reference nonexistent parent node ('EmpManagement', '0004_merge_localtest')"*. Both now depend on `EmpManagement 0002_initial` / `OrganisationManager 0001_initial` (shipped). The packages contain no core-app migration except the initial ones and `EmpManagement 0003_emp_reports_to` (complete install only); the migration graph of the complete install was loaded and checked without errors.

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 83. Security hardening and history cleaning (1.62.0)
sections.text: 1.62.0 builds every item of the review *ZEO Cloud – History cleaning and security* (1.54.0) that belongs in the product. What stays outside the product – the cloud platform (firewall / WAF, private network, central logs, a UAE / KSA region), the penetration test, written policies and ISO 27001 – is listed in 83.10 with what ZEO now gives for it.

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 83. Security hardening and history cleaning (1.62.0) › 83.1 Uploaded files (gap 1)
sections.text:
- Every file saved through a file field is written to a register (`ZeoCloud.MediaFile`: path, company, record). `/media/` opens a file only for a signed-in user **of that company who may open the record** – the same rules as the screens (own records for employees, the reporting manager, branches for branch HR, the add-on apps' own rules, the record of a note or attachment). Other users get 403; without sign-in 401 (as since 1.56.1); company logos stay public.
- Run `python manage.py media_register` once after the update (it links the files that already exist; safe to run again). A file in no record (older generated files) still opens for signed-in users; `ZEO_MEDIA_STRICT=true` limits those to the server administrator.
- New uploads get a random part in the file name (`passport_k3J9xQ2mTzA7.pdf`); `ZEO_MEDIA_RANDOM_NAMES=false` switches it off.
- A token of a signed-out session no longer opens files.

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 83. Security hardening and history cleaning (1.62.0) › 83.2 Hidden self-service fields (gap 6)
sections.text: - An employee reading their own record through the employee API no longer receives the fields HR set to *Not shown in self service*, the hidden groups (family, bank, salary …) or the face-recognition data. HR users still get every field.

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 83. Security hardening and history cleaning (1.62.0) › 83.3 HTTPS, headers, rate limits, tokens (gaps 3, 4, 5)
sections.text:
- `ZEO_HTTPS=true` (when nginx serves https): https redirect, secure cookies (session and CSRF), HSTS one year with subdomains, the https address from `X-Forwarded-Proto`. `manage.py check --deploy` then shows no security warnings (preload is the owner's choice: `ZEO_HSTS_PRELOAD=true`).
- Every API answer: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options DENY`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy`, JSON not cached; uploaded HTML / SVG files are sandboxed.
- `deploy/nginx-zeo.conf`: port 80 only redirects (and serves Let's Encrypt); 443 with TLS 1.2 / 1.3, modern ciphers, HSTS, CSP of the web app, `limit_req` (sign-in and codes 10 a minute per address, API 20 a second); `real_ip` lines for a server behind Cloudflare / a load balancer. **If the API is on another host than the app, add that host to `connect-src` and `img-src` of the CSP.**
- Rate limits in ZEO (429 with Retry-After), per address for doors without a login, per user otherwise: sign-in 20 / minute, codes and links 20 / minute, password reset 10 / hour, exports 60 / hour, searches 120 / minute, paging through the employee API 240 / minute, every signed-in user 600 / minute, without login 120 / minute. Each can be changed in .env (`ZEO_RATE_SIGNIN=…` …); `ZEO_THROTTLE=off` switches them off (load tests).
- Access tokens last **30 minutes** (`ZEO_ACCESS_MINUTES`); the app renews them with the refresh token, which is **spent on every use** (a new one comes back). A spent refresh token that comes back after 60 seconds (two tabs at once are fine) ends the whole session – it may have been stolen – and is a security event. The session's end does not move with renewals (14 days, `ZEO_REFRESH_DAYS`).
- A new password ends every other sign-in of the user.
- Sign-in security ›

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 83. Security hardening and history cleaning (1.62.0) › 83.3 HTTPS, headers, rate limits, tokens (gaps 3, 4, 5)
sections.text: Sessions: sign out after N minutes without use (the app tells ZEO how long the person has not touched it, so the bell and token renewals do not keep a session open); administrators sign in again every N hours and can have a shorter idle time; **a sign-in works only on the device that signed in** (a copied token is refused and the session ends).

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 83. Security hardening and history cleaning (1.62.0) › 83.4 Countries
sections.text: - Sign-in security › Countries: allow ZEO only from a list of countries (AE, SA, OM …), for staff users or everybody – refused sign-ins and requests (403) are security events. The country comes from a free database file on the server (`ZEO_GEOIP_DB`: DB-IP *IP to Country Lite* CSV, or MaxMind GeoLite2-Country with the `maxminddb` package); without it the rule cannot be checked and the page says so. Sign-in alerts and the security dashboard show the country too.

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 83. Security hardening and history cleaning (1.62.0) › 83.5 Give access (employees with and without e-mail)
sections.text:
- Settings › Give access (right *Can give employees access*): the employees (filter *Not activated*), then how the password is set: **send set-password link** (company setting, default 24 hours), **use existing login** (the e-mail has a login of another company), **generate password** (shown once, changed at first sign-in), **code by WhatsApp / SMS** (the company's own gateway), **printed activation slip** (one-time code + QR, valid 7 days, PDF in English and Arabic with a picture guide; a new slip cancels the old one), **kiosk only** (a start PIN the employee replaces at the first kiosk use), **HR types a password** (only when switched on), **company default password** (see below), or **by the rule** for many at once (link / code / slip). Who was missed is listed with the reason.
- HR, payroll and administrator users only get the e-mail link (and the authenticator app). An e-mail domain with single sign-on gets no password. Every way given is in the employee's audit log; a generated password is never stored.
- `/activate` (English / Arabic, big buttons): the employee types the user name and the code of the slip or the message, and chooses the password; *Send me a code on WhatsApp / SMS* also serves as "forgot password" for employees without e-mail.
- Sign-in security › Sign-in ID: **e-mail optional** (employees without e-mail sign in with their code – as before) or **e-mail required** (they sign in with the e-mail; employees without e-mail get no login), per employee category. Self-service employees may now sign in with their e-mail too.
- Company default password (not recommended, off): never "Admin", a common password or the company name; works N days (default 7) after it was given; the first sign-in asks the last 4 digits of the Emirates ID and the date of birth; 3

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 83. Security hardening and history cleaning (1.62.0) › 83.5 Give access (employees with and without e-mail)
sections.text:
wrong tries lock the login until HR unlocks it; never for HR / admin users.
- **A password someone else knows is changed first**: after a sign-in with a generated, typed, company default or other temporary password, the sign-in page asks for the user's own password before anything opens; the server refuses every other request until then (403 `password_change_required` – also for the phone app and scripts using such a login), and the same password is not accepted as the new one. Users still signed in with such a password are sent back to the sign-in page once.
- A kiosk PIN typed by HR is now a start PIN: the employee chooses their own at the first kiosk self-service sign-in (easy PINs and the date of birth are refused).

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 83. Security hardening and history cleaning (1.62.0) › 83.6 Data protection
sections.text:
- **Bank-detail changes need a second person** (off by default): an HR user who adds, changes (bank, account, IBAN, routing code) or removes an employee's bank account gets *saved for approval by a second person* (409); Settings › Bank-detail changes – another person with *Can approve bank-detail changes* (or an administrator) approves or rejects. The employee is told by e-mail and in the ZEO inbox about every change. An employee's own self-service request approved by HR is already two people.
- **Exports**: every export is in the export log (security dashboard). *Exports need a right* (*Can export lists*; employees still export their own data), a row limit above which *Can export large lists* is needed, and a **watermark** (user, time, address) on every PDF – the lists exported in the browser ask ZEO first; PDFs made by the server are stamped by it.
- **Masking**: IBAN / account numbers, Emirates ID and passport numbers as ••••1234 for users without *Can see full bank details* / *Can see full Emirates ID and passport numbers*; salaries as •••• for HR users without *Can see salaries when they are masked* (employees still see their own pay). A masked value sent back by a form is never saved. Exports made by the server are not masked – use the export right for them.
- **Uploads**: programs and web pages are refused (by name and by content); the content must match the name (an image saved as another image type is accepted); size limits per kind; a **ClamAV virus scan** when clamd runs on the server (`sudo apt install clamav-daemon`; `ZEO_CLAMAV=auto` finds it), switchable per company. Refused uploads are security events.

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 83. Security hardening and history cleaning (1.62.0) › 83.7 Password asked again (step-up)
sections.text: - Sign-in security › Ask for the password again: before approving payroll, the WPS / SIF file, bank-detail changes, user rights and exports, ZEO asks for the password (or the authenticator code) again; then the actions stay open for N minutes (default 10). API keys are not asked.

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 83. Security hardening and history cleaning (1.62.0) › 83.8 Log and history retention
sections.text:
- Settings › Log and history retention (administrators or *Can clean logs and history*): one row per category with its rows, MB, oldest entry and what would go now. **System noise** (read inbox items 180 days, read bell notifications 90, WhatsApp / SMS / push log 90, webhook deliveries 30 / 90, automation runs 180, import history 180, export log 365, recently viewed: the last 30 per user, staging / temporary files 2 days) and **audit history** (change history and audit log, approval / configuration audit, "view as" log: 5 years, at least 1 year).
- **Preview** first; **Clean now** needs the company name typed; the **nightly job** (switch on) runs at about 02:05 Gulf time. Rows go in batches of 5,000 within a time limit; what is left goes the next night.
- Audit history is written to a **zip archive** (JSON lines) in `ZEO_BACKUP_DIR/history-archive/<company>/` before it is removed; the archive can be downloaded from the page; each cleaning is a permanent audit-log line.
- **Legal holds** now also for a case (disciplinary case, HR ticket, resignation – its employee is held too) and for the whole company (no audit history is cleaned). History of held employees and cases, and of employees with an open disciplinary case, survives every cleaning.
- Never cleaned: payroll, payslips, WPS, settlements, leave ledger, attendance, approved requests, documents, notes and files on records.
- My sign-in › *Clear my history*: the user's recently viewed records and the searches the browser remembers.

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 83. Security hardening and history cleaning (1.62.0) › 83.9 Security dashboard and e-mails to administrators
sections.text:
- Settings › Security dashboard (administrators): staff users without the authenticator app, wrong passwords of the last 7 days, locked accounts, active sign-ins (address, country, device), API keys, exports of 30 days, administrators, security events of 30 days.
- E-mails to the company's administrators (on by default, Sign-in security › Data protection): a new administrator, permission groups changed, an API key created, single sign-on changed, an authenticator reset, a spent token used again, a sign-in used on another device, 10 wrong passwords in 15 minutes, a sign-in refused by country, a virus found, an export above the row limit refused, Clean now. At most one e-mail an hour per kind and user.
- System health shows HTTPS, the token lifetime, the rate limits, the virus scan, the country database, and whether the last backup was encrypted and copied off the server.

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 83. Security hardening and history cleaning (1.62.0) › 83.10 Backups, and what stays outside the product
sections.text:
- `zeo_backup` encrypts the backup when `ZEO_BACKUP_KEY` is set (AES-256-GCM in 4 MB pieces; `--new-key` prints a key – keep a copy OUTSIDE the server), checks every piece, copies it to `--copy-to` / `ZEO_BACKUP_COPY_TO` (another disk, a mounted share – the copy is checked too) and runs `ZEO_BACKUP_COPY_CMD` (e.g. `rclone copy {folder} offsite:zeo/{name}` to S3 / Azure / B2 with object lock, or `rsync` over SSH). `--decrypt <folder>` gives the plain files back for a restore.
- Outside the product (hosting and process – the review's sections 3.5 – 3.7): firewall / WAF, private network for database and Redis, disk encryption, object lock, central logs and 24/7 alerts, a UAE / KSA region, the yearly penetration test, written policies, ISO 27001. The new nginx file, rate limits, `check --deploy`, encrypted off-server backups and the security events are what ZEO gives for them.

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 84. Journal vouchers or invoices – per company (1.62.0)
sections.text:
Accounting › Settings › Accounting application › **Send documents as** (shown for Odoo and Zoho Books):

| Choice | What goes to the accounting application |
|---|---|
| **Journal vouchers (JV)** – the default, as before | one balanced journal entry per ZEO document |
| **Invoices, bills and payments** | Property rent / service invoices → customer invoices (Odoo `out_invoice`, Zoho `/invoices`, marked sent); credit notes → credit notes; receipts → customer payments **matched to the invoices they pay** (Odoo's Register payment, Zoho `invoices` applied), so the invoices show Paid there; vendor bills → vendor bills |

Payroll, settlements, owner payouts, commissions and refunds always go as JVs – they are not invoices.

How it works
- The lines are the same as the JV: the income / expense lines become the invoice lines (same accounts and analytic), the receivable / payable account is set on the partner, the VAT line becomes the tax. The tax is found by its rate (VAT ÷ base) unless a tax id is entered in Settings (for Odoo the id is a number).
- Totals are checked **before the document is posted**: if the accounting application calculates a different total than ZEO (more than 0.05), the post fails with both figures and the document stays a draft there. A retry finds that draft (it is not made twice) and checks it again – correct the tax on the draft in the accounting application, or delete the draft, then post again.
- A retry never makes two documents: the reference is `ZEO <journal number> <document number>` and it is searched first.
- Reversing a posted journal in ZEO: an invoice / credit note / bill gets a posted credit note (Odoo) or is voided (Zoho); a payment is cancelled (Odoo) or deleted (Zoho Books has no void for payments).
- A receipt for invoices that were sent

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 85. Demo and test data workbook – and the fixes found loading six months of work (1.62.0)
sections.text:
`python manage.py load_workbook <workbook.xlsx> --schema <company>` loads a data workbook into a company: test data, demo data or a migration. The workbook has an **Index** sheet (order, sheet, screen, address, how, phase, run as), a **Columns** sheet (column title → field, so a workbook loads in any language) and one sheet per screen.
- *import* sheets go through the generic import of the list screens (same rights, branch rules, duplicate checks and workflows as the screen; the column titles are the screen's labels, so such a sheet can also be imported by hand with the screen's **Import** button); *api* sheets post each row to the screen's own API; *action* sheets call approvals, posting, payroll runs …
- *setup* sheets load first; *monthly* sheets are replayed month by month (column `@month`), so requests are approved by their real approvers, attendance is recalculated and payroll runs month after month, the way the company would have worked. `@date` moves a record's created time – and on an action row the times the action sets (approved, resolved, issued …) – to the business day.
- `@skip_if` makes a second run safe (it skips what is there); `--check` validates without saving; `--only "Sheet A,Sheet B"`; `--from-month 2026-08` resumes. Rows that fail are listed (sheet, row, reason) and written to `<workbook>.log.json`; the rest is loaded.
- `@until YYYY-MM-DD` on a row for a future day (shift requests can only be for today or later): loaded after that day the row is left out and counted as "date passed"; `{today:+N}` = N days after the load day.
- A sheet with How = `job` runs a daily job of the scheduler (only `maintenance-daily`: the work orders of due preventive plans), so the next sheets find what it made; `--check` does not run it.
- The import now reports a val

The workbook delivered with 1.62.0, **ZEO_Demo_Data_1.62.0.xlsx**, is the demo company *Golden Dune Integrated Services LLC* (two branches, 48 employees, every app) with six months of activity, May – October 2026 – see its *Read me* sheet. Loading it from scratch into a new company found these product faults, all fixed in 1.62.0:

- **Approvals of general requests and document requests silently stopped** in a server process that had run for a while: two signal handlers had the same name as the resignation handler, so only a cache kept them alive; when the cache dropped them, new requests were saved as Pending with no approver. They (and four more handlers with shared names) have their own names now.
- **Self-service on for an employee who already had a login** made a second login named after the employee code and moved the employee to it; the chosen login is kept now.
- **A new install could not create its first company**: workflow rules and history were read while the company's tables were being created (aborted transaction in `ZeoApps 0002`).
- **Split shifts counted one hour short** every day (the gap between the two parts is the break; the attendance rule's break was taken off as well), so overtime was lost.
- **Payroll formula components of both branches** were applied to every employee (paid or deducted twice).
- **Leave opening balances** of one branch were booked on the other branch's leave type when both had the same code.
- **Move-out settlement** counted the owner's unpaid leasing fee as the tenant's, so the deposit refund came out as 0.
- **Clearing a cheque** dated the receipt today

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 86. Print templates – the design of the payslip and every printed document (1.62.0)
sections.text:
**Settings › Print templates** (company administrators and the new right *Design the printed documents* – `manage_printtemplate`).
Every printed document has a gallery of ready-made designs, like a template gallery: **Classic** (letterhead with the logo,
boxed tables, formal title), **Modern** (colour band header, clean tables, summary tiles), **Compact** (dense one-page layout for
printing many), **Bilingual EN / AR** (English and Arabic labels, Arabic letterhead on the right) and, for the payslip, final
settlement and HR letters, **Arabic** (right to left). The company sets any design as the default – for all branches or one branch,
for any language or only English / Arabic – or makes a copy and changes it.

Documents: Payslip · Final settlement statement · Salary certificate · Experience / employment letter · No objection certificate
(NOC) · Salary transfer letter · Offer letter · Warning letter · Loan agreement and schedule · Expense claim · Leave approval letter ·
Asset handover form.

- **Gallery** – live thumbnails (the company's own logo and colours with sample data), Preview with any record of the company,
  Set as default, Make a copy, Edit, Rename, Delete own copies; the samples of ZEO are read only and can be reset.
- **Editor** – a block editor for the common changes (tick and order the blocks: header, title, employee details, attendance,
  earnings / deductions, totals, net pay in words, year to date, leave balance, bank, signatures, footer …; look, header style,
  colours, fonts, logo position, text size, A4 / Letter, portrait / landscape, margins, language) and an **HTML / CSS** tab for full
  control with a placeholder picker (click to insert `{{ employee.name }}` …) and the live preview beside it. Every save is a
  version; any version can be restored.

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 86. Print templates – the design of the payslip and every printed document (1.62.0) › Deploy steps (live server)
sections.text:
1. System packages for WeasyPrint (pango / harfbuzz / fontconfig):
   `sudo apt install -y libpango-1.0-0 libpangoft2-1.0-0 libharfbuzz0b libharfbuzz-subset0 fontconfig`
   (the fonts are bundled in `PrintTemplates/fonts/` and `Translations/fonts/` – no font package is needed).
2. Python packages (in the virtual environment): `pip install -r requirements.txt`
   (new: `weasyprint==70.0` with `pydyf`, `tinycss2`, `cssselect2`, `tinyhtml5`, `Pyphen`, `fonttools[woff]`, and `pypdfium2==5.14.0`
   for the PNG previews – all free / open source: BSD / Apache-2.0 / MIT; fonts SIL OFL 1.1).
3. Check the engine: `python -c "import weasyprint; print(weasyprint.__version__)"` (an `OSError` about pango means step 1 is missing –
   ZEO then keeps printing the old PDFs).
4. Database: the new company app **PrintTemplates** (in TENANT_APPS): `python manage.py migrate_schemas PrintTemplates`
   (or the usual `python manage.py migrate_schemas`).
5. Samples for every company (idempotent; new companies get them automatically at creation):
   `python manage.py seed_print_templates` – after a later product update with new sample designs:
   `python manage.py seed_print_templates --refresh` (refreshes only the samples). Demo company only:
   `python manage.py seed_print_templates --demo gdis` (Modern becomes its default payslip).
6. Language packs: `python manage.py load_language_packs` (Arabic terms of the new screens).
7. Restart the application server (gunicorn / Celery workers) so the payslip e-mail task uses the new attachment.
8. Thumbnail cache: `ZEO_PRINT_CACHE` (default `<project>/print_cache/`) must be writable by the application user; it is not
   served by nginx.

sections.section: ZEO Books – update package, version 1.79.5 (20 November 2026) › 87. Company isolation – a change in one company never changes another company (1.62.0)
sections.text:
ZEO keeps every company in its own database schema, but some lists live in the shared (public) schema and were changed for the
whole server from a company screen. A company administrator who changed the rights of **HR Manager** in *Settings › Permission
groups* changed them for every company on the server (and could delete the group for everyone); a group name could exist only
once on the server; and a few other shared lists had the same fault. From 1.62.0:

**Permission groups (Settings › Permission groups)**
- The standard groups – *HR Manager*, *Payroll Manager* and the app role groups *Projects – …*, *CRM – …*, *Property – …*,
  *Maintenance – …*, *HSE – …*, *Asset Management – …*, *Accounting – …*, *People – …*, *HR operations – …*,
  *Business partners – …* – and any group another company uses are **shared templates**.
- **Saving** a shared group in a company makes the company's **own copy** with the changes ("Your changes were saved in your
  company's own copy. Other companies are not affected."). The copy keeps the name the company sees ("HR Manager"); it is stored as
  "HR Manager [schema]". The company's users are moved to the copy; logins that also work in other companies and invited logins
  (ZEO Cloud company access, Group HR head) get the copy's rights in this company only – their rights elsewhere do not change.
- **Deleting** a shared group from a company is refused with a message. **Deleting the company's copy** puts the company back on
  the standard group (its users are moved back).
- **Group names are unique per company**: two companies can each have an "Accountant" group.
- Everything that looks a group up by name – workflow roles ("HR Manager"), Group HR head, the app role lists, invited logins –
  uses the company's own copy in that company. Group

  Clearing the company's text goes back to the standard one. Platform administrators still edit the shared packs.
- **Logins shared by several companies**: an employee who leaves one company (employee deleted / switched off, or self-service
  turned off) no longer switches off a login that also works in other companies – only the access to this company is removed.

sections.text:
**Settings › Administration › Data workbook** (company administrators; also linked from Import history and the Setup guide) loads a
company's data from one workbook in the ZEO data-workbook format: company details, branches, departments, designations, categories,
salary components, document types, employees, salaries, bank details (IBAN), documents with expiry, leave opening balances and
history (family, qualifications, previous jobs). The six-month demo workbook (`ZEO_Demo_Data_1.62.0.xlsx`) uses the same format.

1. **Template** – *Download the template* gives `ZEO_Client_Data_Template_1.62.0.xlsx`: a *Read me* (the order: company → masters →
   employees → salaries → opening balances → history, and the sheets a go-live needs), the *Index* (sheets in loading order, how each
   is loaded, *Mandatory*), *Columns* (column title → field key), *Columns help* (meaning, required, allowed values, format, example of
   every column), drop-down lists for choice columns, date cells formatted dd/mm/yyyy, and grey example rows marked `example` in the
   `@example` column – the loader never loads them.
2. **Upload** the filled workbook (.xlsx, up to 30 MB).
3. **Check** – every row is really tried, inside one database transaction that is rolled back at the end: nothing is saved, no e-mail
   is sent, and a row that needs a record of an earlier sheet (the employee of a salary row) is checked properly. The result shows
   per sheet what would load / fail and every failing row with the **Excel row number, the column (letter and title), the value, the
   reason and the fix**; *Error report* downloads them as Excel (Summary, Problems, and each sheet's failing rows as in the file with
   `@reason` / `@fix` – correct them there and upload that file again). *Quick check* (option) only vali

4. **Load** – runs in the background with live progress (sheet, month, rows done / failed, time left); the page can be closed. It ends
   with a summary and the error report. Every loaded row is remembered: loading the same or the corrected file again skips the rows
   already loaded (*Load again (resume)*), so a stopped or interrupted load is simply started again; *Options › Load the months from*
   starts the monthly part at a month. *Stop* ends it after the current row. One check / load runs at a time per company.
5. **History** – every check and load: when, who, file, result, error report.

What the loader accepts and explains (also `python manage.py load_workbook`): dates as dd/mm/yyyy, d-m-yyyy, yyyy-mm-dd, 5 Mar 2026
or Excel dates; numbers with thousands commas or "AED"; Yes / No; linked columns by code or name ("not found" says the closest value
and the valid ones; "matches several records" lists them – use the code); column titles as the screen labels with or without the
Columns sheet; unknown columns (with the closest title), missing mandatory columns, sheets missing from the Index (with the closest
name), the same row twice, and @as users that are not logins of the company (a workbook cannot act as a system administrator).

Where it runs: in a Celery worker when one answers, otherwise in a background thread of the web server (`ZEO_WORKBOOK_RUNNER=thread`
forces the thread, `=celery` the worker). A run whose worker went away shows *Interrupted* after 10 minutes – load again.
`python manage.py run_workbook <run id> --schema <company>` (or `--upload <id> --kind load|check`) runs it from the command line.
`python manage.py load_workbook <file> --schema <company> --check` is the same trial from the command line (`--quick-check` the old

sections.text:
Every call takes `?schema=<company>` and a company administrator's sign-in: `Authorization: Bearer <access token>` (POST
`/users/token/`) or, better for a script, an API key made in *Settings › API keys and webhooks* for an administrator, **read / write**:
`Authorization: Api-Key zeo_…` (or `X-API-Key: zeo_…`).

| Call | What |
|---|---|
| `POST /tools/api/workbooks/` (multipart, field `file`) | upload → `201 {id, file_name, rows, sheets:[{sheet, how, phase, rows, examples, months, mandatory, found}]}` |
| `POST /tools/api/workbooks/<id>/check/` `{"quick": false, "only": ["Employees"]}` | start a check → `202` the run |
| `POST /tools/api/workbooks/<id>/load/` `{"from_month": "2026-08", "only": [...]}` | start the load → `202` the run (`409` while another run is busy) |
| `GET /tools/api/workbooks/<id>/` (`?all=1` every error) | the upload, `run` (the last run) and `runs` |
| `GET /tools/api/workbooks/<id>/runs/<run>/` | one run |
| `POST /tools/api/workbooks/<id>/stop/` | stop after the current row |
| `GET /tools/api/workbooks/<id>/errors/[?run=<run>]` | the error report (.xlsx) |
| `GET /tools/api/workbooks/` | uploads and the history of runs |
| `GET /tools/api/workbooks/template/` | the blank template |
| `DELETE /tools/api/workbooks/<id>/` | remove an upload |

A run: `{id, kind: check|quick|load, state: queued|running|done|failed|stopped|interrupted, message, progress: {sheet, month, done,
total, percent, ok, failed, skipped, elapsed_s, eta_s}, totals: {ok, failed, skipped, past, examples, problems}, sheets: [{sheet, ok,
failed, skipped, examples, problems}], error_count, errors: [{sheet, row, column, letter, value, error, fix, level}]}`. A check is
clean when `state = done` and `totals.failed = 0` and `totals.problems = 0`.

```bash
H="Authorization: Api-Key $ZE
```

| Company administrators | Home and the Setup guide show "N steps left before HR transactions open" / "HR transactions open after N more setup steps" with the open steps and Continue. Switch **Allow transactions before the setup is finished** in the Setup guide (e.g. for a trial payroll before go-live). sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 100. Recommended settings: GPSSA by law, leave pay recovery, net pay protection (1.62.3, user request 2 Nov) › 100.1 GPSSA by the law that applies to each employee
sections.text:
1.62.2 (item 41) made the statutory GPSSA scheme the only GPSSA line. The scheme had one rate (11 %), so nationals insured before 31 Oct 2023 would have paid 11 % instead of 5 %. Now the scheme and the pension formula variables use the same rules:

| | Joined before 31 Oct 2023 (old law) | Joined on / after 31 Oct 2023 (Federal Decree-Law 57/2023) |
|---|---|---|
| Employee | 5 % | 11 % (the scheme's rate) |
| Employer | 12.5 % | 12.5 % below AED 20,000 (the government pays 2.5 %), 15 % from 20,000 |
| Contribution salary | 1,000 – 50,000 | 3,000 – 70,000 (the scheme's limits) |

- Every figure is in **Payroll › Legal rates** (new: minimum and maximum for the old law, the employer's full rate and the AED 20,000 limit) – a company adds its own value from a date when the law changes.
- The law is chosen by the employee's joining date. An Emirati first insured with GPSSA at an earlier employer before 31 Oct 2023 keeps the old law – ZEO has no "first insured" date yet (pending list): check such employees.
- Golden Dune GD-0001 (joined 2015): 2,350.00 employee / 5,875.00 employer on 47,000 (1.62.2: 5,170.00).
- Sources: WTW, "United Arab Emirates: changes to social security for new members" (Jan 2024); Crowe UAE, "Key highlights of the new pension law".

- `--apply` writes arrear lines; the next payrolls deduct them as **Salary arrears recovery**, at most **20 % of the payslip's gross a month** (UAE Labour Law: recovery of amounts paid in excess of the entitlement is limited to 20 % of the wage); the rest waits for the following month. An underpayment is paid at once as Salary arrears.
- Arrear lines now wait until the payslip whose period reaches their date (used for the monthly parts; all other lines have a past date and behave as before).
- **Golden Dune GD-0017 (done):** maternity leave DXB-LEA-0009 – the calendar now has 17/09–30/09 and 01/10 at 50 % pay; September was paid for 30 days instead of 23: 7 × (7,500 + 3,000 + 1,000) ÷ 30 = **2,683.33** to recover – **2,425.00** from the October payroll (20 % of 12,125.00) and **258.33** from November. sections.text:
- A day is closed when the employee has a payslip in a processed, approved or paid run whose attendance window contains it (off-cycle and pending runs do not count). The run's window decides, so a 25th cut-off works.
- Applying, the last approval, moving the dates or cancelling a leave that touches closed days answers: **"November salary is already paid for 17/11/2026 – 19/11/2026."** ("already processed" while the run is not paid yet). Only the closed days are named. The same text shows as a warning in the leave check before sending.
- **HR and payroll** (not for their own leave) get two buttons: **Cancel** (nothing saved) or **Add to December salary** – the request is saved and, when it is approved or cancelled, the pay difference goes to the next payroll as arrear lines ("Salary arrears recovery" / "Salary arrears"). A recovery takes at most **20 % of the wage a month** (UAE Labour Law limit for recovering an amount paid in excess, as in 1.62.3); a payback is paid at once. HR's choice when recording the request is kept, so the approver is not asked again.
- **Self service** (and a line manager approving without HR's choice) gets the message only: "… Ask HR or payroll to record this leave."
- Leave after the cut-off (26/11–30/11) goes to the next run with no message.
- Approvals and both cancel paths are saved whole or not at all.

sections.text: Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021, Article 19(3): overtime **between 10 pm and 4 am** is paid at the basic wage plus **at least 50 %**; **workers working on shifts are excluded**. Sources: the law text (MOHRE PDF, mohre.gov.ae); u.ae "Working hours in the private sector"; MOHRE "Workers' rights – Working hours"; Khaleej Times "Overtime pay explained" (Ashish Mehta & Associates). Other countries were not checked and keep their own rule.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 107. Midnight and night rules (1.62.6, pending item 24) › Now
sections.text:
- **Night work without a shift**: a punch closes yesterday's open "in" when it is within the maximum shift length (the rule's maximum hours, else 12 h) and today's own shift is not about to start. 22:00 in + 06:00 out: before two "missing punch" days with 0 h → one present day of 480 minutes.
- **Night window**: a rule still on the standard 22:00–06:00 counts the law's window (UAE 22:00–04:00) while "Count the law's night window" is on (default on in the UAE); a window the company set itself is kept. Night shift 22:00–08:00: 480 → 360 night minutes.
- **Night overtime rate only for workers not on shifts** (default on in the UAE): 2 h overtime on a 22:00–06:00 shift ×1.50 → ×1.25; a worker without a shift 22:00–08:00 keeps ×1.50. A "shift worker" is someone whose planned shift that day is a night shift or runs past midnight.
- Unchanged: a normal day shift, two real days without a shift, a forgotten clock-out, a planned shift 20:00–04:00.
- Setting: Attendance › Overtime law and reasons › Night overtime (law text, two check boxes, the sources).

For the legal adviser: who is a "worker working on shifts" (ZEO's reading above; rotating-roster staff on day shifts?). Pending: the 50 % per overtime hour between 22:00 and 04:00 (ZEO gives the night rate to all overtime on a day with at least 120 night minutes, as before). Days already calculated keep their old night minutes until recalculated.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 108. Accrue now – pay later (1.62.7, pending item 18) › What it does
sections.text:
- **A setting on a salary component**: on / off, the payout month, pay at the final settlement, pay the payout month's own amount in the same run (default on), and the accrual account (default 224005). When on, the component becomes type Others – out of gross and net pay; its old type comes back when the setting is switched off. The setting covers every branch copy of the component (same code). Deductions, Basic, loans, advances, gratuity, PF / ESI / tax and the payout component itself cannot be accrued; a setting without a payout month or final settlement is refused.
- **Payroll**: each month's amount is added to the employee's balance under the run's own salary month (a 29th–28th cut-off is still "January"). In the payout month an automatic line "<component> – payout" (component `<CODE>_PAY`, made by ZEO) pays the balance; a second run in the same month never pays it again.
- **Opening balance** per employee and component with a date, for the go-live (again replaces it; 0 removes it).
- **Final settlement**: "<component> – accrued, paid at exit" = the balance + the amount for the days after the last payroll (worked out as payroll does, with the steps shown); paying the settlement takes the balance to 0.
- **Undo**: deleting or recalculating a run takes back its accruals and payouts; a rejected payslip's rows do not count.
- **Journals**: monthly payroll Dr expense / Cr 224005; payout Dr 224005 / Cr salaries payable; final settlement Dr 224005 for the balance, Dr expense for the days after the last payroll.
- **Report**: Reports › Payroll › Accrued components (opening, accrued, paid by payroll, paid at final settlement, balance); the page Payroll › Accounting › Accrue now – pay later also shows each balance's movements.

UAE IBANs are checked (AE + 21 characters, mod-97). Payroll run › Payments shows each part under its method; the WPS SIF carries only the WPS part (setting "only the WPS part" – default – or "the whole salary", **to be confirmed** with the bank / MOHRE); a held salary comes off the WPS part first. Each instalment is a payslip line with the balance left; the cap and the net-pay controls are kept and the rest carries over; pause / resume, settle early, write off (reason); a rejected or deleted payslip gives the instalment back; the final settlement deducts the balance. sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 125. Companies and databases (1.67.1)
sections.text:
User decisions of 5 November 2026: make a company or an own database inactive / active, delete a company or an own
database (kept 30 days, restored only by a server administrator), and company names unique per user / account like Odoo.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 125. Companies and databases (1.67.1) › A. Make inactive / Make active (company and own database – nothing is deleted)
sections.text:
| What | How |
|---|---|
| Who | The **owner** of the company's ZEO Cloud account (`Account.owner`) or a **company administrator** of the company – a user of it whose rights there are administrator (`ZeoCloud.rights.is_admin`, the same check as `_zeo_is_admin`; an invited login's `CompanyAccess.admin` counts for that company). Other users get 403 / 404. |
| Where | Choose a company › ⋯ › **Make inactive…** – the shared confirm window (`z-confirm`) asks first. |
| History | Who and when: `ZeoCloud.CompanyLife.history` (`made_inactive`, `made_active`, `deleted`, `restored`, `removed`) and, for a company of a ZEO Cloud account, the account history (`AccountEvent`). |
| Inactive company | Nobody can sign in to it or use it: every request with `?schema=<it>` answers **403** `{company_state: 'inactive'}` (UserManagement `SchemaMiddleware`, so screens, API keys and ZKTeco devices alike); the scheduled jobs leave it out. It is not in Choose a company, the top-bar company menu, the sign-in answer (`tenants`), the company list API, the copy sources or the group views of its users. Its owner and administrators still see it on Choose a company marked **Inactive** ("Made inactive by … on …") with **Make active**. A screen that is open when the company becomes inactive goes back to Choose a company. |
| Own database | Settings › Subscription › Databases: **Make inactive** / **Make active** (owner). All its companies are inactive the same way (marked "Its database was made inactive"); they come back with the database. The **default database** can be neither made inactive nor deleted (make another one the default first) – chosen because new companies are made in it. |
| Console Archive | Aligned, not replaced: Adept's console **Archive** (AccountCompany.archived – frees the plan place)

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 125. Companies and databases (1.67.1) › A. Make inactive / Make active (company and own database – nothing is deleted)
sections.text: now also makes the company inactive, and **Restore** makes it active. The owner's Make inactive does not archive: the company keeps its plan place, so Make active always works without a plan check. |

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 125. Companies and databases (1.67.1) › B. Delete company – kept 30 days
sections.text:
| What | How |
|---|---|
| The hole | `DELETE /users/api/company/<id>/` (CompanyViewSet, a ModelViewSet with no permission class) removed the company row at once. It now answers **405** for everyone; the company list / detail API also leaves inactive and deleted companies out. |
| Who | Owner or company administrator (as in A). |
| Confirm window | Choose a company › ⋯ › **Delete company…**: lists what will be deleted (employees, branches, payroll runs, payslips, leave requests, loans, employee documents, users who lose access, pending invitations, uploaded files – counts) and the **Delete company** button opens only when the exact company name is typed. The server checks the name again. |
| Backup first | `zeo_backup --schema <schema> --company-files --no-media --no-status --keep 0 --dir <backups>/deleted --tag company-<schema>` (the existing backup command; new options below): the schema dump and the company's uploaded files, checked, encrypted when `ZEO_BACKUP_KEY` is set. If the backup fails nothing is deleted. The browser of the person deleting **downloads it automatically** (`zeo-backup-<schema>-<time>.zip`: the plain dump, `files.tar.gz`, manifest, a read-me; an encrypted server copy is decrypted for the download). The link works only for that person, for 24 hours. **One copy stays on the server.** |
| Straight away | The company is inactive and hidden from **everyone** – no Deleted list, no restore button for users (also not for system administrators; the life API answers 404). **Every user is unlinked**: `user.tenants`, invited rights (`ZeoCloud.CompanyAccess`), pending invitations (cancelled), branch access (`UserBranchAccess` in the company). A user whose only company it was keeps the login. What was linked is recorded in `CompanyLife.links` for the restore.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 125. Companies and databases (1.67.1) › B. Delete company – kept 30 days
sections.text:
The per-login rights row (`UserTenantPermissions`) is shared by all companies of a login and is not touched. |
| Nothing blocked | The name is free at once (the name rule ignores deleted companies); the licence place (ZeoLicence usage) and the plan counts (`company_links`, usage, user counts) are freed. The deleted company keeps its schema and domain for the restore, so a new company of the same name gets the next free internal name automatically (`company.save`, `company_jobs._schema_for` and `duplicate.schema_for` now skip existing schemas, PostgreSQL schemas and domains). |
| Restore (server administrator only) | `python manage.py restore_company <schema>` (`--list` shows what can be restored), or the Adept console › **Deleted companies** › Restore. The company is active again, the recorded users / rights / invitations / branch access are linked again, and when its name was taken meanwhile by another company of the same account (or of its users, for a company without an account) " (restored)" is added. |
| After 30 days | The daily job (`ZeoCloud.tasks.run_daily` = Celery `zeocloud-daily` = `python manage.py cloud_daily [--date YYYY-MM-DD]`) removes a company whose 30 days have passed (deleted on day D, restorable until D+30, removed on D+31) – on every server, ZEO Cloud or not. |

**Removed after 30 days:** the company's PostgreSQL schema (all its data), the company row, its domains, the user links still left, invited rights (`CompanyAccess`), invitations (`UserInvite`), the account link (`AccountCompany`), its file register rows (`MediaFile`) and its files (files registered only for this company, its logo, a `media/<schema>/` folder if any), its language settings, notification-inbox rows and shared-row owner rows; phones that had it as last company forget it.

**Ke

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 125. Companies and databases (1.67.1) › B. Delete company – kept 30 days
sections.text: pt:** the backup folder on the server (`<ZEO_BACKUP_DIR or backups>/deleted/backup-…`) for 90 days (there is no stored backup retention on the server – the nightly `zeo_backup --keep` is a command-line value – so 90 days; `ZEO_DELETED_BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS` changes it, never below 30), then the daily job removes it; the `CompanyLife` record (name, schema, who / when, history, state "purged"); the account history lines; logins of the users.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 125. Companies and databases (1.67.1) › C. Delete database, with its companies – kept 30 days
sections.text:
| What | How |
|---|---|
| Before | `owndb.remove_db` only retired an EMPTY, non-default database; `drop_retired` dropped it as soon as no old move copy was left (the screen said "after 7 days"). A retired key was used again by the next new database – and so its PostgreSQL database. |
| Now | Settings › Subscription › Databases › **Delete…** (owner) on a database with companies: the window lists its companies and needs the database name typed. A backup of the **whole database** (`zeo_backup --db <key> --company-files …`) is made first and downloaded as in B; every company in it gets the B treatment (inactive, hidden, users unlinked, nothing blocked); the database is retired and dropped **30 days** later. |
| 7 → 30 | Every retired database – also the existing Remove of an empty one ("It is deleted after 30 days") and one retired when an account leaves Premium – is dropped 30 days after `DatabaseServer.retired_on` (a database retired before 1.67.1 starts its 30 days at the first daily run). A retired key is never used again by a new database. The old copies of moved companies keep their 7 days. |
| Restore | Server administrator: `python manage.py restore_database <key>` or the console › Deleted companies › Restore: the database is ready again with the companies deleted with it (a company deleted with its database cannot be restored alone). |
| Default database | Cannot be deleted or made inactive (decision: new companies are made there; make another one the default first). The main database is never deletable. |

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 125. Companies and databases (1.67.1) › D. Company name rule (like Odoo)
sections.text:
A company name is unique only among the companies of the same user / account: the requesting user's `user.tenants` plus the companies of the ZEO Cloud accounts the user owns (for a company made in an account: that account's companies), ignoring case and spacing. Deleted companies do not count. Changed: `CompanySerializer.validate_name` (create and rename), sign-up (no server-wide check any more), `AccountCompanyCreateView`, the console's create, Duplicate company, the test company (sandbox), the copy names of Duplicate database, `setup_zeo` (the "same name = same company, run again" rule applies only when the given administrator already has that company; a `--schema` of a deleted company is refused). A system administrator is a user of every company, so for them the check covers all their companies.

Places that look a company up by name, checked: `UserManagement/serializers.py` validate_name, `UserManagement/views.py` Duplicate, `ZeoCloud/views.py` sign-up and account create (and the console create, which had no check), `ZeoCloud/owndb.py` copy naming, `ZeoAdmin/sandbox.py`, `setup_zeo` – all now use `ZeoCloud.lifecycle.name_clash` (ids). No import, licence or report matches a company by its name: imports and the setup copy use the company id / schema (`company_copy.check_request` by id); the Enterprise licence counts companies (not names); group reports key by schema (`ZeoGroup/services.py`, `views.py` map schema → name for display only); ZKTeco devices by serial → schema. | The % was a guess | `job_progress._copy_probe` set the copy's share of the bar from the **time** only: seconds ÷ (template size ÷ an assumed 256 KB/s, or the time of the last copies), **capped at 95 %** of the step. The copy is 60 % of the whole bar → the bar ran on by the clock, stopped at **57 %** ("almost done") and stayed there until the copy ended, however long. |

sections.text:
| Where | Now |
|---|---|
| Real progress of the copy | `ZeoApps.job_progress.clone_watched()` runs `clone_schema` and, every second from a second connection, counts the relation locks the copying connection holds in `pg_locks` (they only grow, from 0 to ≈ 4.25 per relation of the source; the ratio of the last copy is learned). The bar follows the work: "Copying the ready company template (36 MB, 861 tables)". Used by the sign-up / account company (`ZeoCloud.services.copy_template`), Create company (`UserManagement.company_jobs`) and Duplicate company in the main database (`ZeoApps.duplicate`). Own-database copies keep the old estimate. |
| A copy that waits | `pg_stat_activity.wait_event_type = 'Lock'` for 5 s → "… – waiting for another database task to finish (N s)"; the % stands and no time left is shown. |
| Size without waiting | The template size comes from the catalogue (`pg_class.relpages`), which never waits for a lock. |
| Honest time left | `Progress(learn=…)` keeps the seconds of each step of the last 5 jobs (cache, 90 days; names `cloudjob:clone` / `cloudjob:migrate`, `companyjob:…`). The step weights follow them, the end (`eta`) = the rest of this step at the usual time scaled by this job's pace + the usual time of the next steps. `with_elapsed()` shows **no** time left before the first job of a server, while the copy waits, when the % has not moved for 15 s (`slow`) or when the end has passed (`overdue`) – the screen then says "Still working – no estimate of the time left". Jobs without `learn` keep the old formula, but not from a % that stopped 15 s ago. |

the descriptor, so a tampered browser could send numbers made elsewhere. Use it with the geofence / IP rules, or keep it off.

length (TKT-00001 → series at 1 → TKT-00002); existing rows are never changed. The setup-guide pattern stays for the 28 HR
types. Document numbering screen: only the active apps' series (API `?all=1` for all), the form offers only the active apps'

  administrator installs DB-IP Lite (CC BY 4.0) in `ZEO_GEOIP_DB`, else the browser position the user agreed to share. Sign-in

  companies (an attack on a login of their company); the company administrator flag is per login (shared rights table) –
  a login that is administrator of one company is administrator in every company it belongs to (by design since 1.22; not

  per company already.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 131. Administrators per company, Arabic sign-in e-mails and Print buttons (1.67.7) › 131.1 What it does (summary)
sections.text:
**Administrators per company.** The owner of the company is its administrator by default: the account owner on ZEO
Cloud, or the database creator (the first system administrator) on a server without accounts. That includes companies
made later, and the owner keeps every branch through the 1.67.6 "Company administrators" group. Any other login is an
administrator only where it was made one. Settings › Users has a new column "Administrator in this company" with an
on/off switch, and the owner has an "Owner" badge. Only the owner or an administrator of that company can use the switch;
for everyone else it is read only. Switching a login off in one company leaves its other companies unchanged. The
following are refused, with a message:
- removing the last administrator (409);
- taking the owner's rights, when done by anyone other than the owner (403);
- deleting, switching off or unticking "Active" for the only administrator (409).
The old "Assign permissions" screen now changes the current company only.

**E-mails in the reader's language.** These e-mails go in each recipient's own language, with English as the fallback,
and have an HTML part with dir="rtl" for Arabic:
- the new-sign-in, locked and refused-network e-mails;
- the sign-in code;
- the administrators' new-sign-in e-mail and security e-mails, one e-mail per administrator, sent only to the
  administrators of the company concerned;
- the payslip e-mail.

**Print buttons.** Print is now on Projects (tickets, AMC contracts), HSE (permits, incidents), CRM (quotations, sales
orders), Property (leases, tenant invoices, receipts), Maintenance (work orders), Asset Management (work orders) and
People (development plans). It is in the list's row actions and on the record page, and is shown only when the app is
active and

sections.text:
* The texts inside security events ("X was made an administrator of the company") are stored English sentences; in an
  Arabic security e-mail they stay English (the frame and subject are Arabic).
* The data step of 0015 is meant to run once. Run again later, it would make every login that is an administrator
  somewhere an administrator of all its companies, because the shared flag now means "administrator somewhere".
* The session "admin" marker used for idle and admin-session limits is set at sign-in as "administrator of any company".
  The 2FA "administrators" rule is now per company.
* System administrators (the server-level flag) bypass most checks. When switched off in one company, they are masked
  only in that company's requests (verified). They can still open the server console.
* Inspections, timesheets and projects have no 1.67.6 print document, so they have no Print button.

  design detail and was not changed.
* Groups another company gave a shared login are no longer applied in the login's other companies. This is a fix: until
  now they leaked rights across companies. A company that relied on that leak must give the group in its own company.

| 51 Deduction limit | Payroll › Setup › **Loan and advance settings**: "Limit the deductions of a month to a share of the wage" – ON for UAE companies at 50 % (Decree-Law 33/2021 Art. 25(2); a UAE company cannot set more than 50), off elsewhere. Wage of the month = gross of the payslip. Order: statutory → loans → advances → others (as 1.62.2). A loan / advance instalment that does not fit stays on the loan / advance and is **added to next month's instalment** (DeductionCut); other deductions carry on "Deductions carried over" (DEDCF, 1.62.2). Optional own shares for loans / advances (% of the wage, empty = none – the law sets none). The payslip and the payroll register (Warning column) say why: "Deductions are limited to 4,750.00 of a gross of 9,500.00: the legal limit of 50 % … Art. 25(2)" + "Loan Deduction ZEO-LOA-…: 255.00 not deducted – added to next month's instalment." Recovery schedules (1.63.0) also respect the legal limit. A deleted / recalculated payslip gives its cuts back. |
| 110 Type limits | A request (and an edit) above the loan type's highest amount or over more months is refused with the limit in the message (60 000 / 60 on a 20 000 / 12 type: "The highest amount of the loan type … is 20,000.00." / "… repaid in at most 12 months."). Highest amount and months must be > 0 on the type. |

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 135. Loans, advances and deduction limits (1.67.11, items 51, 110–117) › 135.2 Legal sources (each fact in two or more independent sources)
sections.text:
* 50 % of the wage a month, whatever the reasons: Federal Decree-Law 33/2021 Art. 25(2) – MOHRE law text
  (mohre.gov.ae, "Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021 … and its amendments", PDF); Gulf News "New UAE Labour Law: When can my
  employer deduct my salary?"; Addleshaw Goddard, "Safeguarding payroll … lawful salary deductions … UAE Labour Law" (2026).
* Loans repaid from the wage within that limit, with written consent, **without interest**: Art. 25(1)(a) – MOHRE law text;
  Gulf News "Can a UAE company charge interest on staff loan?" (also Gulf News deductions article).
* "Wage" = basic wage + cash allowances / benefits; "Basic wage" excludes allowances: Art. 1 – MOHRE law text.
* Deduction of amounts owed (loans, overpayments) from end-of-service benefits: Art. 51(7) (MOHRE law text) and Cabinet
  Resolution 1/2022 Art. 29 – Gulf News "UAE gratuity: Can my employer deduct from my end-of-service payments?"; The Law
  Reporters "UAE gratuity deductions …". None states a percentage → company setting, default 100 % of the earnings.
* Not confirmed (so company settings, empty by default – "legal limit to confirm" not needed as they are not applied): a
  separate share for loans / housing loans. Other Art. 25 caps (overpayment 20 %, penalties 5 %, damage 5 days, court debts ¼)
  are listed in the sources but not applied here – there is no penalty / overpayment component category to apply them to (open point).

sections.text:
* Other Art. 25(1) caps (penalties 5 %, overpayment 20 %, damage 5 days' wage, court debts ¼) are not applied separately – no
  component category marks those deductions; the 50 % total applies to them.
* The wage for the limit is the payslip gross; in new companies the gratuity accrual line GTY is an addition shown on the payslip
  (1.67.10 open point) and so raises the limit.
* The employee's written consent is recorded but not required (requiring it would refuse requests made today without it).
* Profit outside the UAE only; profit income is booked at payout (not spread over the months).
* A rejected payslip approved again takes back advance instalments; a limit cut of that payslip is not re-made (edge case).
* Payroll months in the future (tests) list before today's prepayments in the schedule order; real use is unaffected.
* Advance payout has an API and journal but no button on the advance list yet (the loan has "Pay out" on the Loans page).

* **Held salary at exit (C10):** a salary still held when the employee leaves (Payroll › Hold / release salary – held, or set to
  "release in the next run") is now an earning line of the final settlement, "Held salary <month> – not paid yet". Before, the
  leaver was never paid it. Paying the settlement marks the hold Released ("Paid in final settlement FS-…"); no payroll run
  releases it again (a run made while the settlement is open leaves it too). The settlement journal debits it to Salaries
  payable (it was already a cost in the payroll journal of its month), not to an expense account

  reimbursable again (Approved) and the next payslip pays them; before, they stayed "Reimbursed" by a payslip that was never paid.
  Approving the rejected payslip again pays them with it again – refused when a report was paid another way since
  (`ExpenseManagement/services.py`, `PayrollManagement/signals.py` restore_consumed_items, `PayrollPlus/payslip_reject.py`).
* **Rejected payslip – deductions carried over (C10):** with "Keep net pay at or above 0" deductions that did not fit are carried
  to the next payslip. A rejected payslip now puts the carry-overs it took back to waiting (before: lost in the rejected
  payslip) and parks the carry-over it made (before: deducted again on top of the re-run). Approving it again undoes this

   company-wide standard report for administrators and one per branch-limited user. Any signed-in user of the company could open
   these files by their address – a self-service login read the company-wide employee report – and the report lists showed every
   user's files to anyone. Now the company-wide file opens only for administrators, a per-user file only for its user, and the lists
   show a non-administrator only their own file and the saved named reports (`zeo/media_auth.py` report_file_allows,
   `AccessControl/access.py` BranchReportMixin.filter_queryset).
2. **Users list shown to every login (F6):** Settings › Users asks /users/company-admins/ for the users and their administrator flag;
   any login of the company – also a self-service user – got every user with e-mail. Now only the user's own row unless the user
   manages administrators or has the users right (`ZeoCloud/admin_views.py`).
3. **Holiday calendar given twice (F2):** Assign holidays accepted the same calendar for the same branch / department / category /
   designation / employee again and again (Assign weekends already refused this). Refused now with "The branch already has this
   holiday calendar." (`calendars/serializer.py` HolidayAssignSerializer.validate).
4. **Projects – Management and Service KPIs (F4):** the Management role ("every dashboard and report") was refused on Projects ›
   Service KPIs and the service reports, and the menu entry was hidden. New right key `kpi_view` (support manager or the Management

sections.text:
The 1.67.20 package was installed into an **empty database** exactly as INSTALL.md says. `setup_zeo` stopped while it made the
company's tables: the old data migration `ZeoMasters 0008_fill_accounting_ready` failed with "column ZeoMasters_uom.unece_code
does not exist" and the company was not created (an existing server is not affected – its migration ran long ago). The
migration now fills the unit / country codes inside a savepoint like its other part, so an error there can no longer stop the
new company (`ZeoMasters/migrations/0008_fill_accounting_ready.py`; no new migration, the file name and its operations are the
same). Rerun on the same empty database: `setup_zeo` created "ZT Install 1720 LLC" (schema `ztinstall1720llc`): branch Head
office, 22 leave types, National Service Leave nationals only, Gratuity as Others not on the payslip, apps HR, payroll,
projects, the e-invoice unit column present; `load_language_packs`, `load_standard_translations` (535 records),
`collectstatic`, `migrate_schemas` (nothing left to apply), `fix_default_gratuity` (0 to fix), `check` (no errors); What's
new answers 1.67.20, the Projects customers import template and the setup guide answer.

sections.text:
Version 1.67.21 = 1.67.20 + pending item **1.62.8 "Separate Notifications and Approval rules for each app + administrator's
combined view"**. Before, the approval flows and notification templates of every app were one shared list under Settings ›
Automation, and the built-in approval levels, escalation and e-mail templates of HR and Payroll were spread over many menus.
Now every app has its own two pages, and the administrator keeps one view of all apps. **How approvals and e-mails run is not
changed** – the pages only group the same rules by app (checked before and after, 145.4).

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 146. Payroll open points closed (1.67.22 – pending C3, C7, C11, C12, C13, C14) › 146.2 C3 – salary payments posted to accounting, split shown on the payslip
sections.text:
* **Payroll run › Payments › Mark paid** now makes a journal (source "Salary payments"): Dr Salaries payable (the payable
  account of the payroll journal) / Cr the paying account of the method – WPS, bank transfer and cheque: the bank (1010, or the
  bank account of Loan and advance settings); cash: cash on hand 1000; a company method: its own mapping. One journal per
  "Mark paid", dated the day paid, with the payment reference. **Not paid** on a line already journaled makes the opposite
  journal ("Salary payment undone"). Setting the whole run to **Paid** journals the parts not marked yet, once.
* Accounts: **Accounting › Accounts › Salary payments** – one row per payment method (key `paid_<method>`, by branch too).
* Built only with Accounting › Settings › "build the journal when a payroll run is approved" on (the same switch as the payroll
  journal). What was journaled is kept in the run's payment store – no new table.
* A split salary (Payroll › Salary split) shows **Paid in parts** on the payslip PDF (English, Arabic and bilingual) and in the
  print templates (`payslip.paid_parts`, Bank block of the payslip designs).
* The message after Mark paid names the journal ("Journal JV-… posts the payment to accounting").

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 146. Payroll open points closed (1.67.22 – pending C3, C7, C11, C12, C13, C14) › 146.3 C7 – Ramadan in payroll's planned hours, Ramadan break
sections.text:
* Attendance › Ramadan: new **Break on a Ramadan day (minutes)** (empty = each shift keeps its own break, 0 = no break,
  up to 240). The attendance engine uses it for the break deduction and the overtime schedule of Ramadan days.
* Payroll: the planned hours of the month (`standard_hours`) count each Ramadan working day with its shorter hours; with no
  shift planned, 160 h less the Ramadan reduction per Ramadan working day. New formula variable `ramadan_days`. Salaries are
  not reduced – an hourly rate worked out from `standard_hours` is higher in Ramadan.
* Legal basis (two sources): MOHRE announcement 15/3/2022 and Gulf News on Cabinet Decision 1/2022 Art. 15(2) – working hours
  in the private sector are reduced by 2 hours a day in Ramadan; hours worked beyond them are overtime (Decree-Law 33/2021
  Art. 19, Khaleej Times). The dates are still entered each year from the MOHRE announcement.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 146. Payroll open points closed (1.67.22 – pending C3, C7, C11, C12, C13, C14) › 146.4 C11 – loans and advances on a pay calendar (weekly, every two weeks, twice a month)
sections.text:
* Payroll › Loan and advance settings › **Employees on a pay calendar**: *Whole instalment in the period that closes the month*
  (default – as before) or *A share of the instalment in every period*: monthly instalment × 12 ÷ periods a year (weekly 12/52,
  every two weeks 12/26, twice a month 1/2); the last share takes what is left; the deduction limit applies to each payslip.
