sections.text:
* A new company had no salary component that pays **approved overtime**, **expense reports "with the payroll"** or **approved leave
  encashment** (open point of 1.67.15, 139.5): they were approved and then waited for ever. The country defaults (setup_zeo and
  Setup guide › Start › "Apply the country defaults") now add, only when no component pays them yet:
  * **Overtime** (OT) = `basic_salary / standard_hours * ot_weighted_hours` – the basic wage per planned hour × the approved hours ×
    the rate of the overtime policy (UAE Decree-Law 33/2021 Art. 19: overtime on the basic wage plus 25 % / 50 %); only approved
    overtime counts, and the pay structure still decides attendance or HR-entered overtime;
  * **Expense reimbursement** (EXPREIMB) = `expense_reimbursement_amount`;
  * **Leave encashment** (LVENC) = `leave_encashment_amount`.
  Every employee with a salary gets them (0 when there is nothing approved). HR can change the formulas.
* **Existing companies:** nothing changes by itself. Check with payroll first, then Setup guide › Start › "Apply the country
  defaults" adds the missing ones.

sections.text:
* **Recalculate keeps the run (P-BUG-08 / 12).** Payroll run › Recalculate makes the payslips again in the same run: same id and
  page address, same document numbers, the preparer and the history kept; the history shows "Recalculated the payroll – n payslip(s)
  before, n after". Before, the run was deleted and a new one made (new address, new numbers, history lost). The payslips' loans,
  recoveries, expense reports, holds and monthly inputs are given back as before; the AI audit of the run is removed (it described the
  old payslips). Refused with the reason for an approved / paid run, a run whose payslips were sent for approval, and an off-cycle
  run (changed on its own page). API: `POST payroll-plus/api/workspace/runs/<id>/recalculate/` (`GET` lists the recalculations).
* **Payslip PDF with text (P-BUG-10 / 32).** Download and Save PDF on the payslip page take the PDF made on the server (the company's
  payslip design, else the standard payslip) – searchable text in English, Arabic or both as Payroll controls › Payslip language
  says (`?lang=en|ar|en_ar`). Before, the page made a picture of the screen. API: `GET payroll/api/payslip/<id>/pdf/`;
  `POST payroll/api/payslip/<id>/upload-pdf/` with `make=true` keeps the server PDF on the payslip.
* **Hour quantities are no employer cost (P-BUG-26).** An "Others" monthly input that holds hours or days used by another
  component's formula (e.g. overtime hours) is no longer counted as employer cost on the run page and posts no journal line.

  off-cycle and pay-cal

  decided in 1.62.4 (item 67), the days not approved stay leave without pay: 2 of 5 days of annual leave approved → 2 days paid
  from the balance, 3 days unpaid on the payslip. A company administrator can act on the rows of the leave register too.
* **My leave tiles (L-BUG-14):** a zero balance of a leave type outside the employee's leave policy is no tile.
* **Approvers tab (L-BUG-16):** the texts of Leave policies › Approvers say who gets a request when a role is empty, that a request
  never goes to the employee who asked, and that only a "No approval" type is approved without an approver.
* **Reporting manager list (L-BUG-17):** only working logins, with the designation, in name order; the employee being edited is not
  offered as their own manager.
* **A new employee can be deleted (L-BUG-18):** the zero leave balances and empty salary rows ZEO makes by itself are no "use"; an
  employee with no transaction is deleted for good (before: kept as inactive although the button said Delete); an employee with
  transactions is deactivated as before.
* **Dialogs opened from a row (L-BUG-19):** a dialog opened from a list's Actions cell (e.g. Translate on Leave types) no longer
  inherits the cell's one-line text – its texts were cut off at the right.
* **Probation in months (L-BUG-20):** a probation of 30, 60 … 180 days counts in calendar months – 180 days from 1 January ends on
  1 July (was 30 June). Other numbers of days count in days. A confirmation date the form worked out before the update (in days)
  is still recognised as the form's own date,

sections.text:
* **Social security summary** – GPSSA, GOSI and the other statutory schemes (Payroll › Statutory schemes): contributory salary, employee and employer share per employee and month; group by Scheme for the total to pay each authority. A scheme whose lines are 0 for the employee is not listed.
* **Loss of pay summary** – per payslip: payroll days, paid days, days without pay (unpaid leave, absence, before joining / after leaving) and the pay lost on the components that deduct leave.
* **Data for payroll** – before the run: per employee the days without pay, absent, late, approved overtime, shift days, on-call days and every monthly input the payroll formulas will read, with the attendance window of the month.
* **Payroll liability summary** – what the runs of the period owe: net salaries payable (paid / not paid yet, from Payments), salaries held, each statutory scheme (employee + employer share) – and to whom.
* **Payroll journal** – the accounting lines (account, debit, credit, department) of the payroll and salary payment journals of the runs.
* **Salary withhold** – every salary hold of the period: held, released, still held, why, last action and by whom.
* **DIFC DEWS contributions** and **ADPF pension contributions** – the year by employee and month (DEWS also shows the gratuity still owed for the service before DEWS).
* **Salary bands** – the monthly salary against the grade's minimum and maximum: compa-ratio and position in the band.

sections.text:
* **Settings › API keys and webhooks › Webhooks:** a webhook can be limited to chosen branches ("Only these branches"). None ticked = every branch, as before.

sections.text:
* **Accounting › Posting rules and connection › Branch connections (optional):** a branch can post its journals to its own Odoo database / company or Zoho Books organisation, with its own address, database, login, key and (optionally) journal code. The keys are encrypted and never shown again.
* The posting rules, accounts and dimensions stay the company's – only where the journal goes changes.
* Once a branch has an active connection, journals are made **per branch**: one journal for each branch with its own connection, and one for the rest of the company. Each is balanced, and together they are the same as the single journal before. Payroll, provisions, settlements, expenses and the other sources are split by the branch on their lines.
* If some lines have no branch, the journal stays whole and goes through the company connection, with a note.
* Posting a branch journal (and its reversal) uses the branch's connection.
* Switching a branch connection off, or removing it, makes the open journals again as company journals; the open branch journal is cancelled ("Replaced"), so nothing is posted twice. Posted journals are never touched.
* **Test** checks a branch connection and keeps the last result.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 152. Optional connections per branch (1.67.28) › 152.5 Found and fixed in the tests of this version
sections.text:

* `migrate_schemas` on a server with more than one company could record the migrations of this version without making the new table / columns in the companies.
  * **Cause:** while a company was migrated, a record saved by the migration's own steps fired the record webhooks. Their lookup read the new column before it existed. The failed query, although caught, spoiled that company's migration transaction.
  * **Fix:** the webhook lookup now runs in its own savepoint and is not cached on failure.
  * **Tested:** updating the 1.67.22 install from the package now makes the table and columns in every company (way 1 below).

sections.text:
Version 1.68.0 = 1.67.28 + items 29 – 40 of the pending list, in the new page **Payroll › Payroll extras** (and six reports).

**Migration:** the new app `PayrollExtras` (0001, new tables only). No core app is migrated.

**Code-only change in a core app:** PayrollManagement `signals.py` gives the payroll formulas the new variables (153.4, 153.5).

**How amounts reach the payslip:** everything that pays goes through Payroll › Monthly inputs, so the payslip, the WPS file, the payroll journal and the reports carry the amounts like any other input. The first time, components ZCOMM (Commission), ZSVC (Service charge share) and ZRETB (Retention bonus) are made: addition, variable, marked as monthly input. They can be renamed.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 153. UAE payroll extras (1.68.0, pending items 29 – 40) › 153.2 Commission and incentive plans (item 29)
sections.text:
* **Plan:** set on the sales amount, or on the % of the target reached. Each plan has tiers and an optional cap per month.
* **How the tiers work:**
  * progressive slabs, e.g. 2 % up to 50 000 and 3 % above;
  * the whole amount at the rate of the slab reached;
  * a fixed amount per slab.
* **Monthly entry:** HR enters the month's sales (and target) per employee. The commission is worked out with its breakdown.
* **Approve and send to payroll:** writes it as the employee's monthly input for that month.
* A sent entry cannot be changed.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 153. UAE payroll extras (1.68.0, pending items 29 – 40) › 153.3 Retention / deferred bonus with clawback (item 31)
sections.text:
* **Award:** amount, award date and the payroll month it is paid in, then "Send to payroll" (monthly input ZRETB).
* **Clawback:** if the employee leaves within the clawback months after the payment, the amount to repay is added to the **draft final settlement** as a deduction line "Retention bonus repaid". It is either the whole bonus or pro rata to the months not served, and is added once per bonus. The bonus is then marked "clawed back".
* An exit after the clawback period repays nothing.

sections.text:
* **Hourly / daily pay:** an employee can be paid by the hour or by the day, with the rate and (part time) the contracted hours a week. The payroll formulas get:
  * `hourly_rate`, `daily_rate`;
  * `is_hourly`, `is_daily`;
  * e.g. a component `worked_hours * hourly_rate`.
* **GCC nationals' pension:** GCC nationals working in the UAE pay into their home scheme through GPSSA. The five countries are pre-filled but **switched off**.
  * HR checks each country's rates and wage base with GPSSA, ticks "checked" and switches the country on.
  * Formulas then get `gcc_pension_emp`, `gcc_pension_er` and `gcc_pension_base` for employees of that nationality.
  * Oman: 7.5 % employee / 11 % employer from 1 January 2024 (two published sources).
  * The other countries come from one published source and are marked "confirm with GPSSA".

* Sources: dubai.ae; Ius Laboris.

sections.text:
* **HR:** Reports › Leave & attendance › **Employee leave statement**. Pick the employee (leavers too) and the year.
* **Employee:** Self service › **My leave statement** (and Leave › My leave statement). Only their own statement.
* Per leave type:
  * the balance brought forward on 1 January;
  * earned, taken, cancelled leave returned, encashed, carried forward, lapsed, yearly reset, adjustments;
  * the balance on 31 December.
* Then every line of the year with the balance after it and the note.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 154. Printed reports, leave statement and punch map (1.69.0, pending item 21) › 154.5 Punch map
sections.text:
* Attendance › **Punch map**: the active geofences (circles with their radius) and the punches of a day that carry a location.
* Green = inside a geofence, red = outside, grey = no geofence applies. Clicking a row of the list under the map zooms to the punch.
* For each punch: the nearest geofence that applies to the employee and how many metres outside its edge.
  * A geofence tied to employees applies to those employees only.
  * Otherwise the geofences of the employee's branch (and those with no branch) apply.
* "Only the punches outside" shows the exceptions. The counts show inside, outside, without a location and the geofences.
* Void punches are left out. The branch switcher limits the employees and geofences.
* For HR users with attendance rights; others get 403.
* The map tiles come from OpenStreetMap (as on the Geo fence screen); the server only sends coordinates.

sections.text:
Version 1.70.0 = 1.69.0 + the country rules of pending items 142 – 151 for branches in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, Qatar and India.

**The UAE rules are not changed.** A branch takes the rules of its country (Settings › Branches › Country, or the rule set applied to the branch); everything below applies only to those branches.

**Migration:** PayrollPlus 0021 (two choice lists: the GOSI scheme on the employee's pension details and the "Basic + housing" contribution base). No core app is migrated.

**Code-only changes in core apps:** EmpManagement `utils.py` (the end-of-service record takes the country gratuity), DashboardManagement `reports.py` (the Gratuity report).

Every legal fact was checked in two sources (listed in 155.9). Where only one source was found, or the sources differ, ZEO marks it **"confirm"** on the settlement and in these notes – check it with a local adviser before relying on it.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 155. GCC and India country rules (1.70.0, pending items 142 – 157) › 155.2 End-of-service gratuity on the country's basis (items 142, 143)
sections.text:
| Country | Wage used | Per year | Minimum / resignation | Nationals |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Saudi Arabia | wage with the fixed allowances (basic, housing, transport …) | half a month for 5 years, a month after | employer ends: any service; resignation: under 2 years none, 2 – 5 one third, 5 – 10 two thirds, 10+ full | Saudis also get the award |
| Kuwait | wage with the fixed allowances | 15 days for 5 years, a month after; capped at 18 months' wage | resignation: under 3 years none, 3 – 5 half, 5 – 10 two thirds, 10+ full (**confirm** the half and full bands) | – |
| Bahrain | wage with the fixed allowances | 15 days for 3 years, a month after (rule set) | 1 year | Bahraini and other GCC nationals: no gratuity (SIO pension) |
| Oman | basic wage | service before 31/07/2023: 15 days for 3 years, 30 after; from 31/07/2023: 30 days | 1 year | Omanis: no gratuity (Social Protection Fund) |
| Qatar | basic wage | 21 days (rule set) | 1 year | Qataris: no gratuity (**confirm**) |
| India | "wages": basic + DA, plus the allowances above 50 % of the pay (Code on Wages) | 15 days ÷ 26 (rule set), ceiling ₹ 20 lakh | 5 years; fixed-term contract (Employee › Identity: Limited) 1 year for exits from 21/11/2025 | – |

* The final settlement shows the calculation step by step (years, days, wage, daily wage, share, cap). The end-of-service record and the Gratuity report give the same figure.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 155. GCC and India country rules (1.70.0, pending items 142 – 157) › 155.3 Bahrain – SIO end of service (item 144)
sections.text:
* From 01/03/2024 the employer pays the SIO an end-of-service contribution for non-Bahrainis: **4.2 %** of the wage a month in the first 3 years of service, **8.4 %** after. The SIO pays the award for that service.
* New statutory scheme **"SIO end-of-service contribution (non-Bahrainis)"** (code `sio_eos`, employer only), added by Settings › Country settings › Apply country defaults. ZEO switches 4.2 % → 8.4 % by the employee's service.
* The final settlement pays the gratuity only for the service before 01/03/2024, with a note that the SIO pays the rest.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 155. GCC and India country rules (1.70.0, pending items 142 – 157) › 155.4 Oman – savings scheme (item 145)
sections.text:
* From **19/07/2027** the employer pays **9 % of the basic** a month to the Social Protection Fund for non-Omanis, replacing the gratuity for that service. The gratuity of the service before stays owed (paid at exit on the last basic, as before).
* New statutory scheme **"Savings scheme for non-Omanis"** (code `om_savings`, employer only); it charges nothing before 19/07/2027.
* The final settlement and the Gratuity report stop the gratuity on 18/07/2027 for exits after that date.
* The other Social Protection Fund rates are unchanged in ZEO (the sources do not agree on the split – **confirm** in Payroll › Statutory schemes).

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 155. GCC and India country rules (1.70.0, pending items 142 – 157) › 155.5 Saudi Arabia – GOSI (item 146)
sections.text:
* Contribution wage = **basic + housing** (not transport), between SAR 1,500 and 45,000, for the annuities, SANED and occupational hazards.
* **First insured from 03/07/2024** (Royal Decree M/273): annuities 9 % + 9 %, rising 0.5 % each side every 1 July from 2025 (9.5 % 2025, 10 % 2026, 10.5 % 2027, 11 % from 2028). Insured before: the scheme's rates (9 % + 9 %).
* The day first insured is entered on the employee (Employee › Employment › Social insurance (GOSI), scheme "GOSI (Saudi Arabia)"); empty = the joining date decides. The page shows the rate in force.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 155. GCC and India country rules (1.70.0, pending items 142 – 157) › 155.6 Final settlement due date and deduction limit (items 150, 151)
sections.text:
* **Due date:** Saudi Arabia 7 days after the last working day when the employer ends the contract, 14 days on resignation (art. 88); India 2 working days (Code on Wages). The earlier of the law and the company setting is used. Other countries: the company setting.
* **Deduction limit (Loans and advances › Settings):** new Saudi companies start with 50 % of the wage (arts. 92 – 93); Kuwait companies 25 % with loans 10 % (**confirm**). The limit cannot be set above the law. Existing settings are kept.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 155. GCC and India country rules (1.70.0, pending items 142 – 157) › 155.7 Not in this version (still on the pending list)
sections.text:
* Item 147: Kuwait PIFSS tiers; item 149 (GCC nationals in another GCC state) is in 1.68.0 (Payroll extras › GCC nationals' pension).
* Item 152: wage and bank files (Mudad, Qatar / Oman WPS, Bahrain WPS 2.0, Kuwait bank file, India NEFT) – the official file specifications are not public; a bank's or authority's specification is needed for each. The existing Bank file layouts can be used meanwhile.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 156. Document Center and document expiry alerts (1.70.1) › 156.2 The folder tree (Documents › Document Center)
sections.text:
One tree for the whole company:

| Root | What is in it | Who sees it |
|---|---|---|
| **General** | company folders; the old Document library moved here with its folders and files (each file = version 1.0, numbered LIB-yyyy-nnnn) | the old library rights carry on (view / add / delete folder and document), plus the rights given on the folders |
| **My folders** | a private folder for each user; they make subfolders, upload and share them | the user; others only through the rights the user gives |
| **HR › Employees** | a folder per employee, "code – name", made and renamed from the record; it also lists the documents on the employee record (read-only there) | users with the employee-document rights, within their branches; **each employee sees their own folder** (read only) |
| **Projects**, **Business partners** | a folder per project / partner | users with the project / partner rights |
| **Property › Buildings**, **Assets**, **HSE › Sites**, **CRM › Accounts** | a folder per building, asset, site, account – only when the app is active | users with that app's rights, within their branches |

* System folders (roots and record folders) cannot be renamed, moved or deleted. Users create their own folders wherever they have the "Create folders" right.
* Upload one file (with its details) or a **zip** (its folders become subfolders; blocked file types are skipped and listed); download a folder as a zip (only what the user may see).

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 156. Document Center and document expiry alerts (1.70.1) › 156.3 Rights
sections.text:
* The 13 rights of the SOP: view, create folders, upload, edit, review, approve, publish, download, print, share, archive / delete, dispose, manage rights.
* Given on a folder (or one document) to a **user, permission group, branch, department or everyone**, as a preset – **viewer** (view, download, print), **contributor** (+ create folders, upload, edit), **reviewer** (+ review), **approver** (+ approve, publish), **manager** (+ share, archive, manage rights) – or as single rights.
* Subfolders inherit the rights of the folders above; "inherit" can be switched off per folder.
* The creator of a folder manages it. Only a Document Center administrator (company administrator, or a user with the new permission "Configure the Document Center (categories, workflows, numbering, all folders)") gives "Dispose".
* **Confidentiality** on each document: public, internal, confidential (only its owner, the people named on it and reviewers / approvers of the folder), restricted (only its owner and the people named on it). Only public documents can be shared outside by users.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 156. Document Center and document expiry alerts (1.70.1) › 156.4 Registration, numbering, categories
sections.text:
* Each document has a number, title, folder, category, owner, department, branch, the linked employee / project / partner, received / effective / expiry dates, confidentiality, tags, remarks and the category's own fields (text, number, date, list; required or not).
* **Categories** (Settings tab): code, numbering pattern from `{company} {branch} {dept} {cat} {yyyy} {yy} {mm} {seq:4}` (default `{dept}-{cat}-{yyyy}-{seq:4}`, e.g. HR-POL-2026-0001), restarting every year, month or never; an approval workflow; default confidentiality; expiry date required; retention in years (kept-until date from the effective date).
* The same file uploaded twice is pointed out (checksum).

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 156. Document Center and document expiry alerts (1.70.1) › 156.5 Versions
sections.text:
* Every new file is a version: 1.0, then 1.1 (minor) or 2.0 (major). The version before becomes **superseded**. A version can be **restored** (it becomes a new version) and two versions **compared** (lines added and removed, for PDF, Word and text files).
* **Check out / check in**: while a document is checked out, only that user uploads a version.
* Readers see the version in force; drafts are for the people who work on the document and its reviewers / approvers.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 156. Document Center and document expiry alerts (1.70.1) › 156.6 Review, approval and publishing
sections.text:
* A category with a **workflow** makes its documents *controlled*: draft → under review → pending approval → approved → **published**. Stages are review or approval, decided by named users, a permission group, the owner's line manager or the department head; one of them or everyone; with days to decide.
* Approvers get a to-do; they approve, return for correction or reject (with the reason). A returned draft is corrected and sent again under the same version number.
* A published controlled document is locked: its details are fixed and a change is a new revision, which goes through the workflow while the published version stays in force. Publishing the revision supersedes the old version and sends it to the people who had the old one.
* Documents without a workflow are in force as soon as they are uploaded.
* Waiting for me: the approvals, the documents to read / acknowledge, the documents returned, the user's documents expiring within 30 days, what they checked out.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 156. Document Center and document expiry alerts (1.70.1) › 156.7 Distribution, links, lifecycle
sections.text:
* **Distribute** a published document to users, branches or departments, with or without a **read acknowledgement**; the list shows sent, opened and acknowledged.
* **External links**: valid 1 – 90 days, optional download limit, can be withdrawn; the page opens without signing in and gives the version in force; every opening and download is logged.
* **Archive**, **make obsolete**, back in force; **dispose** (the files are destroyed, the register entry and the log stay). Documents of employees under a legal hold cannot be deleted or disposed of.
* **Trash**: deleted folders and documents are kept 30 days, then removed by the daily job (02:40). The daily job also marks documents past their expiry date "Expired" and reminds approvers of overdue steps.
* **Search**: words in the number, title, tags, remarks and the text inside PDF, Word and text files; category, status, department, confidentiality, upload and expiry dates – only what the user may see.
* **Activity log** of each document and folder: uploads, versions, views, downloads, decisions, rights, moves, links.
* **Overview**: documents by status and category, waiting and overdue approvals, expiring and expired, not acknowledged.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 156. Document Center and document expiry alerts (1.70.1) › 156.8 Document expiry alerts (Settings › Doc. expiry alerts)
sections.text:
Fixed (the nine points found when the document functions were explained):
1. Only the **current** document of each type is checked (a replaced card no longer alerts) and only **active** employees.
2. The **identity details** (passport, visa, Emirates ID, labour card …) alert like the document rows.
3. The alert's **branches, departments, categories and designations** are applied.
4. Each document is told **once when it enters the window** and **once when it expires** (within the alert's "days after"), not every day.
5. Each alert sends **its own summary** to **its own users**.
6. The e-mail templates are found by their name ("Employee Notification", "User Notification"; the old name "ESS User Notification" too).
7. The built-in texts get their values (name, document, number, dates dd/mm/yyyy, the list of documents).
8. The run is once a day from 09:00 in the company's time zone (the job checks every hour).
9. The user's first name in the summary comes from their employee record (the user has no first name of their own).

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 157. HSE: PPE, emergency, equipment, contractors, matrix size, 15 industry packs (1.70.2) › 157.2 PPE (HSE › PPE, emergency & equipment › PPE issued / PPE catalogue and stock / PPE matrix)
sections.text:
* **Catalogue:** code, name, category (head, eye and face, hearing, respiratory, hand, foot, body, high visibility, fall protection), standard (e.g. EN 397), sizes, life in months, stock, minimum stock, reusable.
* **PPE matrix:** which PPE each job or activity needs – the basis for issuing and for the PPE checks.
* **Issue** to an employee or to a contractor worker (one of the two). Refused when the stock is short, the size is not offered or the contractor worker is blocked. Replace-by = issue date + the item's life.
* The person confirms with **I received it** in ZEO; HSE sees the date.
* **Replace** takes stock again (with the reason). **Return**: back to stock only for a reusable item in good condition.
* Daily: PPE past its replace-by date becomes **Expired – replace**; HSE is told when an item falls to its minimum stock.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 157. HSE: PPE, emergency, equipment, contractors, matrix size, 15 industry packs (1.70.2) › 157.3 Emergency management (Emergency plans, Emergency team, Assembly points, Emergency equipment, Emergency drills)
sections.text:
* **Plans** per scenario (general evacuation, fire, gas leak, chemical spill, bomb threat, medical, flood, power failure, heat stress, rescue from height, confined space rescue, man overboard) with the response procedure, how the alarm is raised, the target evacuation time and the external contacts. A fire, evacuation, gas, spill or bomb plan needs an assembly point. Only the HSE manager approves a plan; **approved plans are open to every employee**.
* **Team:** incident controller, fire warden, first aider, warden, spill responder, rescue team. A fire warden needs a valid "Fire warden" competency and a first aider a valid "First aid" one, when the company tracks them.
* **Equipment** (extinguishers, alarms, AEDs, first-aid kits, eye wash, hose reels, sprinklers, gas detectors …): next inspection = the last one + the interval. A **defect** raises a repair action with an owner and a due date. Overdue inspections and services are reported daily.
* **Drills:** not in the future. Over the target time, a wrong head count or a weak rating means **improvement needed**, and such a drill closes only once an action is raised.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 157. HSE: PPE, emergency, equipment, contractors, matrix size, 15 industry packs (1.70.2) › 157.4 Equipment safety and certificates (Safety equipment and certificates)
sections.text:
* Lifting gear, scaffolds, harnesses, cranes, forklifts, MEWPs, ladders, pressure vessels, power tools … with **green / yellow / red tags**.
* Yellow needs the restrictions written down. Red needs a repair owner and the due date, and puts the equipment out of service.
* An **expired certificate turns the tag red** (on save and in the daily job). A new valid certificate marked "passed" puts the equipment back in service. A certificate that has already expired, or expires before it was issued, is refused.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 157. HSE: PPE, emergency, equipment, contractors, matrix size, 15 industry packs (1.70.2) › 157.5 Contractor workers and performance (Contractor workers / Contractor performance)
sections.text:
* Workers of a contractor (a business partner) with induction, medical and cards. **Cleared to work** = active, inducted (induction in date), medical in date when tracked, and the contractor approved. The ID / passport number is shown to HSE only.
* **Score:** 100 points, less 15 per lost-time injury, 5 per other incident, 5 per suspended permit, 10 for an expired licence or insurance, and a share for workers not cleared; audits weigh 40 % when there are any. **A ≥ 85, B ≥ 70, C ≥ 50, D below.**
* Only the HSE manager finalises an evaluation. A C or D rating can suspend the contractor.

sections.text:

* The risk assessment screen draws the matrix at its size. **HAZID** and **HAZOP** are new assessment types.

Mining; warehousing and logistics; hotels and restaurants; facilities management; agriculture; food processing; marine and ports; aviation; telecom; electrical and utilities; waste; cleaning and pest control; laboratories and pharma; shipyards; data centres.

Each pack adds permit types with their checklists, inspections, drills, toolbox talks, hazards, incident categories, competencies, KPIs and an audit. Installing a pack only adds content. sections.text:
From the handoff (before it reached us): custom-module whole numbers stored as "6E+1"; safe actions skipped the company guards; the Arabic file would have changed 25 existing translations (removed); linked records showed the wrong field; lookups were text in formulas; one administrator could approve their own money action with two administrators; the app-kit apps (CRM, Property, Maintenance, Asset Management, People) could not be written by scripts; a change ignored by an app looked successful.

Found and fixed in our tests of this version:
* **Scripts on records of other apps did not run on a production server** (gunicorn with several workers): each worker kept its own list of these scripts for 30 seconds, so a script made or switched on in one worker was silent in the others – a CRM lead or a Projects ticket saved right after did not start it. The development server has one process, which hid it. A change of a script or of Developer mode now marks the company in the shared cache (Redis); every worker compares the mark on each save (one Redis read, about 0.1 ms) and reloads its list when it changed, so the very next save uses the script. (A first version re-checked every 2 seconds; the test saved a ticket at once after making the script and found it silent again – hence the check on each save; then 58 / 58 three runs in a row.)
* nginx did not send `/developer/` to Django on a server set up from `deploy/nginx-zeo.conf`: the Developer pages answered 405. `developer` is added to the sample (158.11).
* The Developer page showed "1.74.0" next to its title; it shows the ZEO version that brought it (1.70.3).
* The What's new texts of 1.70.3 had no Arabic – added.

sections.text:
Development without programming, on ZeoFlow's custom modules and Blueprint (1.67.26, Settings › Custom modules):
* "Create a vehicle request module with vehicle type (car, van or bus), from date, to date, destination, purpose and the cost, approved by
  the line manager then HR" → the module's fields with their types (read from the words: dates, amounts, numbers, e-mail, phone,
  employee, yes / no, long text, a list in brackets or "a, b or c"), its numbering (VR-0001 …) and its Blueprint: Draft → Submitted →
  one approval step per approver (Approve / Reject, each by the right person) → Approved, with Back to draft after a rejection.
* With the company's AI the design is asked for as JSON from any wording ("I need staff to ask for a gym membership …"); without it the
  rules above read it. Either way ZeoFlow's own checks run on the preview (the same as the Custom modules screen).
* Shown first (fields, Blueprint, flow); Confirm makes it with ZeoFlow's own API; recorded "via Ask ZEO"; Undo deletes it while it has
  no records (a module with records is kept – switch it off on its screen).
* "Add a field driver needed (yes/no) and a field passengers (number) to the vehicle request module" → the new design as a preview;
  existing records keep their data; Undo puts the old design back.
* Company administrators only, and the switch "Ask ZEO may change setup".

Together with 1.71.0 – 1.73.0 this is the whole implementation cycle in Ask ZEO: **setup** (go-live check, app setup checks, data
quality fixes, policy → leave setup), **data migration** (client files mapped to the data workbook, checked and loaded) and
**development** (custom modules), every change as a preview to confirm and undone in one click, plus product and scope questions
answered from the ZEO guides.

sections.text:
Version 1.70.5 = 1.70.4 + **a document date and a posting date on every accounting journal** (pending item "Document date + posting date on every document that makes an accounting entry").

**Migrations:** ZeoAccounting 0011 (the journal's document date, "posting date set by a user", "books closed up to"), ZeoProperty 0006 (invoice date of billing records, approval date of commissions, the vendor's invoice date of purchase orders), ZeoAssets 0006 (posting date of depreciation runs), PayrollPlus 0022 (the date of a recovery settled early / written off). Each fills the dates of the existing records. No core app is migrated.

**Code-only changes:** ZeoAccounting (`services.py`, `views.py`, the Odoo and Zoho connectors), ZeoProperty (`complete.py`, `models.py`), ZeoAssets (`app.py`, `views.py`), PayrollPlus (`recoveries.py`), Chatter `nav.py`; frontend: Payroll › Setup › Accounting journals, the menu hint of the accounting integration.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 160. Document date and posting date (1.70.5) › 160.2 Two dates on every journal
sections.text:
* **Document date** – the date of the source document: the last day of the payroll month, the invoice / receipt / refund / payout date, the vendor's invoice date, the approval date of a commission, the day a recovery was settled, the last day of a depreciation period, the date of a final settlement (paid on, else the last working day), the end of the expense or provision period.
* **Posting date** – the date of the entry in the books. It starts as the document date (payroll: the run's payment date when it has one, as before; final settlement: its accounting date when set, as before). Nothing falls back to "today".
* Accounting journals: the columns **Posting date** and **Document date**; a journal posted in another month than its document is marked **≠**.
* **Change the posting date** on a journal that is not posted yet ("(change)" next to the date). The new date is kept when the journal is checked or built again. A posted / exported journal is never changed – reverse it.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 160. Document date and posting date (1.70.5) › 160.3 Books closed up to
sections.text:
* Settings of the accounting integration › **Books closed up to** (empty = no period closed).
* A journal whose posting date is on or before it is held ("To fix", with the reason) until its posting date is changed; it cannot be posted or marked as exported. A reversal cannot be dated into it.
* Asset Management uses the same date for its depreciation runs when the accounting integration is used (it also works alone).

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 160. Document date and posting date (1.70.5) › 160.4 The right dates from the apps (wrong sources corrected)
sections.text:
| Source | Before 1.70.5 | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Property billing record (invoice / credit note) | the **due date** | the **invoice date** – the day it is issued (new field; old records: the day they were made); the due date goes to the accounting app as the due date |
| Property vendor bill (purchase order) | the **order date** | the **vendor's invoice date** – asked when the invoice is matched (required, not in the future) |
| Property commission | the day the record was **made** | the day it was **approved** (new field) |
| Recovery settled early | a date **read out of the note text** | the entry's own date (new field; old entries: from the note, else the day they were made) |
| Depreciation run | the last day of the period | the posting date of the run (new field, default the last day of the period; not before the period starts) |

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 160. Document date and posting date (1.70.5) › 160.5 To the accounting applications
sections.text:
* **Odoo:** journal entries dated with the posting date; invoices and bills with `invoice_date` = the document date and `date` (accounting date) = the posting date, the due date apart; payments with the posting date.
* **Zoho Books:** journals dated with the posting date, the document date in the notes when it differs (Zoho journals have one date); invoices and bills with the document date; payments with the posting date.
* **Excel / CSV export:** "Date" stays the posting date (the column the import templates use); **Document date** is added as the last column. The ZEO API (journals for other applications) adds `document_date`.
* The Assets journal export has the posting date in "Date" and the document date in the last column.

sections.text:
Version 1.70.6 = 1.70.5 + **the screens take "today" from the user's own calendar, not from the UTC clock** (found in the tests of 1.70.5, section 160.7).

Before, many screens worked out today's date with the UTC clock. In the UAE (UTC+4) that is still yesterday between 00:00 and 04:00, so for example on 16/11 at 01:30 the vendor's invoice date was offered as 15/11, Punch map opened on 15/11 and a new HSE action was due 14 days from 15/11. A date picked in a calendar could also be sent as the day before.

**No migration. Frontend only.** A new shared helper (`shared-ui/z-dates.ts`) gives the local day, the local month and "today + n days"; 78 places in 51 screens use it.

sections.text:
A category's own fields (until now text, number, date and list) get **the 20 types of the form designer**: text, long text, whole number, decimal number, amount, percentage, date, date and time, time, Yes / No, dropdown, multi-select, radio buttons, e-mail, phone, web link, file, employee, rating (1–5) and colour – with **help text, default value, hidden, read-only, section and order**, and the designer's checks (lowest / highest, length, pattern, "show only if", "show on").

* **Hidden** – not shown on the forms; the values stay. A hidden field cannot be required without a default value.
* **Read-only** – shown, filled only by its default value or by a Document Center administrator.
* The values are checked by the same rules as the form designer's (a wrong e-mail, phone, web link, rating, percentage, colour, date or choice is refused with the field's message). Dates are kept as dates, Yes / No as yes / no, a multi-select in the order of its options, an employee as the HRMS employee (code and name), a file as the document's attachment.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 162. Document Center fields like the form designer (1.70.7) › 162.3 Fields of every document and folder fields
sections.text:
* **Document Center › Settings › Fields:** "Fields of every document" – shown on every document, whatever its category; "Folder fields" – shown in every folder's details.
* **The document window:** the category's fields, then the fields of every document, by section. **Add field** and **Arrange fields** (Document Center administrators) open the form designer there; "Fields of the category …" changes the category's own fields from the document. The record bar stays off in the Document Center windows (1.70.1).
* **The folder:** "Folder details" with the folder fields and "Save folder details" (the folder's edit right); "Add / Arrange folder fields" for administrators.
* **New category / category window:** "Add fields" / "Change the fields" open the same designer; the fields are saved with the category.
* A field's label can be changed – the values stay. Its type can be changed only when the saved values fit the new type. Deleting a field deletes its values. A category field cannot have the name of a field of every document.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 162. Document Center fields like the form designer (1.70.7) › 162.4 Upload, search and export
sections.text:
* **Upload:** the fields start with their default values; required ones must be filled (a required file is added right after the document is made).
* **Search:** a **Field** filter with its value (a list for dropdowns and Yes / No) – numbers and dates exactly, text by words; the value shows in its own column.
* **Export to Excel** (new): the found documents with number, title, folder, category, status, version, confidentiality, owner, dates and **one column per field** (the "show on: export" setting is followed; hidden fields are left out).
* The API gives the values in `fields` and the definitions in `field_defs`; search takes `f.<field>=value`; values may be sent by label too.

sections.text:
* **Web link fields (every form designer field, not only the Document Center):** any single word (e.g. "zeo") was accepted as a web link. A web link now needs a domain with a dot – `zeo.ae`, `https://www.zeo.ae/page`, Arabic domains such as `موقع.امارات`, or `localhost`. Values saved before stay; they are checked when they are next changed.
* **The form designer's tick boxes did not tick (every form designer: employee, asset, the screens' extra fields, now the Document Center):** a click anywhere inside the designer window was cancelled by the window's own "click outside closes" handler, so Required, "Read-only for employees" and the "Show on" boxes could not be changed with the mouse. Fixed in the designer; the same slip fixed in the field help settings window and in the HR pages' document preview (links and text boxes inside them).
* **A company administrator could be shown another user's rights on about 160 screens (e.g. Settings › Form designer: "You do not have the right to see this page"):** these screens read "my rights" as the first row of the rights list, and for an administrator that list holds every user's row in no fixed order. The signed-in user's own row now always comes first (OrganisationManager, code only – no migration). Users who are not administrators were not affected (they only get their own row); the server always checked the rights of every change.

A project nothing refers to goes with its own set-up rows (profile, finance, stages, member rates, empty Document Center folder). HSE keeps a "Deleted" line in the record history. Rights: delete customer / AMC contract / ticket / project (Projects permissions); incidents – HSE manager; observations and actions – HSE staff.

sections.text:
The update had stopped the ZeoAdmin, ZeoCloud and OrgStructure save handlers from acting on the rows that record migrations; the ZeoDeveloper handler of 1.70.4 (scripts on records of every app) did the same and looked up its settings without a savepoint while the company's tables did not exist yet. sections.text:
Version 1.73.6 = 1.73.5 + phase 3 of the Document Center:

* **Expiry reminders and escalation.** Each category says when the reminders go (default 90, 60, 30, 15 and 7 days before the expiry date) and who renews: the document's owner or a named user. The Document Center's daily job gives the renewal owner a to-do at the nearest step reached (once per step; a missed day is caught up once, not for every step). When the document has expired and has not been renewed after the category's escalation days (default 7), the escalation user – or the Document Center administrators – get a to-do. New tab **Expiry & renewal**: the documents expiring within 30 / 60 / 90 / 180 / 365 days (and expired ones not renewed) with the days left, the renewal owner, the last reminder and the renewal.
* **Renewal.** **Renew** on a document with an expiry date: the file of the renewed document and the new expiry date (it must be later). The renewal is filed in the same folder with the same category and details, linked both ways ("This is the renewal of …", "Renewed by …"). When it is in force – at once, or after its approval workflow – the old document becomes Superseded and its reminders stop. A document is renewed only once.
* **Retention.** A category's retention now counts from the date it chooses: registered, effective, expiry or archived; "Keep until" is worked out on every change. At the end, the category says what follows: review, archive or dispose – the administrators get a review to-do. **Retention review** (administrators): keep it (reviewed again in a year), archive it, or go on to dispose of it.
* **Legal hold.** A Document Center administrator or a user with the Dispose right sets a legal hold with its reason; the document is then not disposed of and not emptied from the trash. Ho

sections.text:
Version 1.73.7 = 1.73.6 + a simpler, safer payroll setup:

* **Payroll categories** (Payroll › Setup). The 21 system categories (Basic, HRA, Housing, Transport … Loan, PF, Tax) keep their keys – the calculations read them – and get editable English / Arabic names, a report header and an order. Companies add their own (Site allowance, Fuel …), each behaving like a system category. * **Leave categories** (Leave › Setup): the 8 system ones (Annual, Sick, Casual, Maternity, Paternity, Compensatory, Bereavement, Unpaid) and the company's own (Hajj, Study …), each behaving like a system one – a category like Annual counts as annual leave everywhere (leave liability, encashment, gratuity).

Totals are the same either way.

sections.text:
Version 1.73.9 = 1.73.8 + Document Center phase 4 (four new tabs in Documents):

* **Checklists.** The documents each kind of record must have – employees, projects, business partners, buildings, assets, HSE sites, CRM accounts – one document category per item (required or optional, "needs an expiry date"); a checklist can be for some branches (and, for employees, some departments). A record's folder shows its checklist: received, missing, expired, no expiry date or to review (subcategories count). **Missing documents** lists every record of the kind with a gap, with "Ask for them".
* **Upload links (external portal).** From a record's folder (Ask for documents) or from Missing documents: the person's name, e-mail, message, the documents asked for and how long the link works (1–90 days). The person opens the link – no account, phone-size page – and sends each file (PDF, photo or Office file up to 20 MB; the server's upload guard still checks every file). Each file lands in the record's folder in its category as **Submitted** and the sender gets a to-do; it counts in the checklist only once **accepted** (rejecting asks for the reason and opens the link again for that item). The link is "All received" when everything is in; it can be withdrawn; expired and withdrawn links say so.
* **Templates and forms.** Controlled templates (Document Center administrators): HTML with merge fields (`{{ company }}`, `{{ today }}`, `{{ record.name }}`, `{{ employee.name }}`, `.code`, `.designation`, `.department`, `.branch`, `.nationality`, `.joined`, `.email`) and questions to fill in (text, long text, number, date, list – `{{ answer.<key> }}`). sections.text:
Version 1.73.10 = 1.73.9 + Document Center phase 5:

* **Scans are read (OCR).** A photo (JPG, PNG, HEIC, TIFF …) or a scanned PDF without its own text is read on the server with Tesseract, in English and Arabic (free, nothing leaves the server), up to 20 pages a file. Files up to 3 MB are read when they are uploaded – from the Document Center, an upload link, a template or a signature; bigger ones and the files that were there before by the daily job of every company. Each version says where its text comes from – **Text from the file**, **Text read from the scan**, **No readable text** or not read yet – and an editor may **Read the text again**. Settings › Reading scanned documents shows the counts, the languages and "Read the waiting scans now". The words read are searched like any other text: the filter search, search in words, compare two versions.
* **Search in words** (Search tab, above Search with filters). Type a question as you would say it – "Khalid's passport", "expired trade licences", "contracts 2025", "جواز سفر خالد". The categories (and their subcategories), the employees (by name or code), expired / expiring soon / drafts and a year are understood and shown as filters; the other words are looked for in the title, number, tags, fields and the text of the files (also as OCR reads them – 0 for O, 1 for I). Each result gives the sentence found, "read from the scan" when it is, and opens with a click. Only the documents the user may see are searched.

Version 1.73.12 = 1.73.11 + the fixes the team made on 1.73.1 after its full manual test (10 employees, 3 payrolls) – their "1.73.1 → 1.73.2" patch, merged on top of 1.73.11 (only the version number and What's new needed a hand merge):

* **Air ticket allocations: Approve / Reject.** A new allocation stayed "Pending" for ever (no screen could approve it), so the employee's air ticket request was refused ("no approved entitlement"). Payroll › Air tickets › Allocations now has Approve and Reject on a pending allocation (HR with the change or approve right, or an administrator; asked first). Only a pending allocation can be decided; a rejected one is no longer active; the approver is kept as "allocated by" when empty. API `POST /payroll/api/airticket-allocation/<id>/approve/` and `/reject/`.
* **No more false "No access".** A slow or failed rights request (a cold server) was remembered as "no rights" for the whole session, so pages such as Resignation approvals showed "No access" to their approver. The failure is no longer kept, and while the rights are not read the menu does not lock the page – the server still refuses or limits the data.
* **Resignation approved e-mail.** Approved, auto-approved and approved-by-the-manager resignations used the template "request_approved", which sent nothing; they now use "resignation_approved".
* **Final settlement by finance.** The Payroll Manager group gets "validate" and "pay" on final settlements (check – send for approval / send back to HR, and mark paid); approving stays with the approve right and one person still cannot do two steps. Existing companies: `python manage.py payroll_manager_rights --apply`.

Version 1.73.13 = 1.73.12 + the team's "create from drop-down" patch (their 1.73.5), merged on top of 1.73.12 (on 8 screens changed since their base only the two import lines needed a hand merge):

* **"+ Create new <master>…" in every drop-down that lists a master**, on every screen of every app – departments, designations, leave types, salary components, shifts, customers, projects, CRM accounts, HSE sites … When the master you need is missing, choose the last entry: a small form opens with the master's required fields; the record is saved through the master's own API (its checks, rights and numbering, exactly as on the master screen), added to the screen's list and chosen in the drop-down.
* **How it finds the master.** Every list a screen loads is remembered with the API it came from (an HTTP interceptor and a small wrapper of `fetch`); the drop-down's values are matched to that list. The server (`zeo-masters/api/quick/meta/?src=…`) says whether this user may add to that API and with which fields (a DRF list API: from its serializer and its own permission check for a POST; a kit app's options list: from the register of that model). Nothing is created by the meta call.
* **Not offered:** filter bars and list headers, read-only or disabled drop-downs, fixed choices (no list behind them), people and logins (employees, users), companies and branches, transactions (requests, runs, logs …) and masters whose required fields are more than a quick form (over 8) – those open on their own screen. A drop-down can opt out with `data-zqc="off"` or name its list with `data-zqc-src`.

Version 1.73.14 = 1.73.13 + the team's "1.73.3 → 1.73.6" patch (which includes their 1.73.4 dashboard look and 1.73.5 drill-down, date filters, customizing and themes), merged on top of 1.73.13 (four screens needed the "+ Create new" import line merged by hand):

* **Default dashboards.** Nine dashboards are made once per company for the apps it uses – Company, HR, Payroll, CRM, Property, Maintenance, Asset management, HSE, Projects & support – shared with everyone. A dashboard that was deleted is not made again. They are made the first time an administrator opens Reports › Dashboards, or at once with `python manage.py zeoinsights_defaults [--schema <company>]`.
* **Dashboard page.** A themed hero with the dashboard picker and themes, a date filter (presets and custom range) for the whole dashboard, a menu on each card, **drill-down** – a click on a bar, a slice or a row opens a drawer with the records behind it (search, export, open the full report) – and Customize (move cards by drag and drop).
* **App homes.** CRM, Property, Maintenance and Assets get the new design (themed banner, gradient KPI tiles that open their records, bars showing each share, coloured lists); HSE, Projects and the HR home get the banner. **View dashboard** on every app home opens that app's dashboard (only for people who may open Reports › Dashboards).
* **Self-service hero** on Home › My dashboard: photo or initials, role, branch, years of service and manager, quick actions and six live tiles that drill down to the records.
* **Rights.** Cards run as the viewer; a dashboard shows only the cards the person may run, and one with none of them is hidden. A card load counts once against the user's rate limit, not twice.

sections.text:
Until 1.73.15 the server worked out "today" as the server's own day (UTC). In the Gulf that was **yesterday** between 00:00 and 04:00, and a branch in Riyadh or Bangalore shared the head office's day. 1.73.16 works like Odoo and Zoho People: the time zone is chosen per **user**, else the **branch**, else the **company**. There is no time zone per employee: an employee's day is their branch's day.

| # | Where | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Language menu (top bar) › **Time zone** (new) | No choice; dates followed the server. | **Automatic** (your branch, else the company), or a zone you choose. The menu shows "Today" in that zone. Saved on your user. API: `GET/PUT /language/api/my-timezone/`. |
| 2 | Every screen and API ("today", "this month", due dates, ages, expiry checks) | The server's UTC day: 518 places in 181 files used it. | The signed-in user's day: their own zone, else their employee record's branch, else the company. |
| 3 | Daily jobs (reminders, accruals, expiry alerts, payroll schedules) with nobody signed in | The server's UTC day. | The company's day: Settings › Company › Time zone, else the country's, else Asia/Dubai. |
| 4 | Attendance (punch, device, kiosk, import, shift and work day) | Punches were dated in the company's zone, and a device's local time was read in it. | A punch's day, its shift and a device's local time follow the **employee's branch zone** (the branch › Registration and site details › Timezone). A punch at 12:00 UTC is on the 15th for a UTC+14 branch and on the 14th in Dubai. |
| 5 | Every page that needs a right (menu by rights) | If the server was too slow to answer the rights check (team 1.73.12), the page was opened anyway. | The check is tried again once. If there is still no answer, the page is **not** opened: **"Cou

The last open point of Ask ZEO (A9; A1 – A8 came in 1.70.4). An AI tool – an assistant, an agent, any app that speaks MCP – can now read ZEO with API v1 (as before) and **propose** changes. ZEO works each proposal out the way Ask ZEO does and keeps it as a **draft**; nothing changes until a company administrator approves it.

| # | Where | What |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Settings › API keys | Four new scopes: **modules:write** (custom modules and fields), **reports:write** (reports), **workflow:write** (ZEO Developer scripts: reminders, automations), **settings:write** (setup such as leave policy lines, data fixes, changes from a sentence). They need a key that is not read only. The API v1 table on the page lists the new endpoints. |
| 2 | `POST /api/v1/ai/changes/` `{scope, request, language}` | The request in plain words (at most 2000 characters) → **201** with the draft(s): title, before / after rows, state `preview`. **422** when no change came out of it (Ask ZEO's answer says why, e.g. the company's AI is needed to write a script). A proposal of another kind than the scope allows is kept as *cancelled – outside the key's scope*. |
| 3 | `GET /api/v1/ai/changes/` (`?state=`), `GET …/<id>/`, `POST …/<id>/withdraw/` | The key's own drafts and changes; another key's are not found. A draft not yet approved can be withdrawn. |
| 4 | Settings › Ask ZEO › **Waiting for approval** (new) | Each draft with the key, the scope, the request in the tool's words and every record and value before / after. **Approve** makes it as the administrator (the screens' own checks run); **Reject** keeps it in the log as rejected. The company switch "Ask ZEO may change setup" is for Ask ZEO's own users: an administrator's approval is enough for a draft from an AI tool. |
| 5 | Safety | A key can n

sections.text: Version 1.75.0 = 1.73.25 + the first of the five new apps of 18 Nov (Inventory 1.75 → Sales 1.76 → Purchase 1.77 → Accounting 1.78 → Manufacturing 1.79): **ZEO Inventory**, a new app on the app kit. It keeps stock of the items of the shared item master (Masters › Items) in warehouses, values it, and sends the stock journals to the Accounting outbox. The other apps will post their stock through it (Sales: deliveries, Purchase: goods receipts, Manufacturing: consumption and output).

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 191. Inventory (1.75.0) › 191.1 How it works (design)
sections.text:
* **Ledger, never edited** (as Microsoft Business Central): every quantity move (*StockMove*) and every cost amount (*StockValue*, with its own valuation date) is kept. A posted document is corrected only by **Reverse** (a reversing document). The value at any past date is the sum of the cost amounts dated up to it – later postings never change it.
* **Costing method per item** (Inventory › Item stock settings; the company default in the set-up): moving average, FIFO, standard cost, lot (each lot its own cost), serial / specific (each unit its own cost). **LIFO** only when the set-up ticks "offer LIFO" – it is not allowed under IFRS (IAS 2.25) and is for management reports.
* **Costing level** (as SAP's valuation level / Sage 300): one cost per item for the company, per branch or per warehouse. Fixed once stock has moved.
* **Cost adjustment**: the cost of every outflow is worked out again by replaying its item's moves in date order. A back-dated receipt, a reversal or a landed cost that changes what a delivery should have cost adds a cost amount (adjustment) dated on the delivery – or on the first open day when that period is closed. Returns and reversed receipts leave at the cost they came in with.
* **Landed cost** (freight, insurance, customs duty, clearing, port, demurrage, inspection, local transport): split over the goods receipts by value, quantity, weight, volume or by hand; the part on stock still held raises its cost, the part on stock already used goes to cost of sales (as Dynamics / NetSuite). Preview before posting.
* **Accounting**: *perpetual* – every cost amount is a journal (at once, at day end, or on request) in Accounting › Journals (source "inventory", ready to post): receipt Dr Inventory / Cr GRNI, delivery Dr COGS / Cr Inventory, adjustments, scra

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 191. Inventory (1.75.0) › 191.1 How it works (design)

p, count variance, internal use, price variance (standard), revaluation, landed cost clearing. *Periodic* – no stock journals; at the month end **Closing stock JV** books the change in the stock value against "Change in inventory" and closes the period.
* **Accounts**: 16 account roles with default codes (Inventory 1400, GRNI 2150, COGS 5000 …), changed per company, per item category and / or warehouse in **Account sets**.
* **Period close** (perpetual): runs the cost adjustment, posts every cost amount and closes the stock period; nothing can be dated on or before it afterwards. Reopen: manager or administrator, latest period first.
* **Inventory ↔ GL reconciliation** at any date: stock valuation against the GL balance of each inventory account, with what is not yet posted.

sections.text: Version 1.75.1 = 1.75.0 + two changes asked on 19 Nov: (1) the payroll of a large company no longer hangs the system, and the screen shows the calculation as a count of employees; (2) HRMS features other than the standard ones are off for a new company – including the approval hierarchy.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 192. Large payrolls and HR features (1.75.1) › 192.1 Large payrolls in the background
sections.text:
**Why it hung.** The payslips of every employee were calculated inside the web request that saved the run. With 1,000+ employees that request ran for minutes: the web server ends a request after 300 s (gunicorn `--timeout 300`), so the run was lost, the browser kept "Calculating…" and the web worker was busy for everyone else.

**Now:**
* "Calculate payroll" (and **Recalculate**) saves the run and returns at once. The **Celery worker** (`zeo-celery` service of the installation) calculates the payslips. Without a worker answering, the web server calculates them in a background thread – nothing to configure.
* Saved in **batches of 100 employees**, each committed on its own: a failure keeps the payslips already made; the run page then shows "N employees of this run have no payslip yet" with **Continue calculation**, which calculates only those employees (no payslip twice).
* **Live count**: the dialog and the run page show "Calculating **500** of 5,000 employees", the employee being calculated, how many a minute and the time left; Payroll runs lists every calculation running in the company (any user) and the run card says "Calculating 500 of 5,000 employees". The user may leave the page; the preparer gets a notice in the inbox ("Payroll calculated" / "Payroll calculation stopped").
* While it is calculated the run is **locked**: no approval, recalculation, deletion or second calculation (409 "This payroll is still being calculated").
* Runs of 50 employees or fewer are still calculated in the request (the page opens with the payslips, as before); a run of more than 300 employees goes to the background even from another screen or the API.
* Settings (optional, `.env`): `ZEO_PAYROLL_BACKGROUND=auto|celery|thread|off` (default auto; off = as before), `ZEO_PAYROLL_ASK_MIN=50`

sections.text:
* **Ledger, never edited** – a posted entry is corrected only by a reversal (an entry the other way). Each entry balances (debit = credit) or is refused with the difference; headings take no postings; control accounts (customers, suppliers) need the partner on a manual line. Numbers per journal (GJ-, INV-, BILL-, RCT-, PAY- …, or Settings › Document numbering).
* **Years and periods** – the financial year (start month in the set-up) with twelve periods: open, closed (only the finance manager posts) or locked; a lock date for everything on or before it. **Year end** closes income and expenses into retained earnings and makes the next year.
* **Invoices and bills** – customer invoices and credit notes, supplier bills and debit notes, lines with item (shared item master), account, quantity, price, discount, VAT code and cost centre. Posting: invoice Dr customers / Cr revenue / Cr VAT output; bill Dr expense / Dr VAT recoverable / Cr suppliers. A credit or debit note settles its original first. The same supplier invoice number twice is refused. Register a payment from the invoice.
* **VAT (UAE)** – codes for standard rated 5 %, zero rated, exempt, out of scope, reverse charge on imported services (the VAT both ways, boxes 3 and 10), imported goods through customs (boxes 6 and 10), blocked input tax (a cost, not recoverable), recoverable %. Each line carries its VAT 201 box; sales by the place of supply (emirate, boxes 1a–1g).
* **VAT 201** – the boxes from the posted books (amount, VAT, adjustment columns; 8 and 11 totals; 12 due, 13 recoverable, 14 payable); adjustments on the return; **Filed with the FTA** clears the VAT accounts into "VAT payable to the FTA". Due 28 days after the period. (Box structure confirmed from two sources – see 193.5.)
* **Receipts and payments**

sections.text:
– allocated to invoices / bills (by hand or oldest first), the rest on account; **post-dated cheques** held in "PDC received / issued" and moved to the bank on the cheque date (by the daily job, or "Cheque cleared"); **returned cheque** reverses the receipt and opens the invoices again; transfers between bank / cash accounts.
* **Foreign currencies** – invoices, payments and banks in another currency with the rate of the date (Exchange rates); the difference between the invoice rate and the payment rate is a realised gain / loss; **Exchange revaluation** at a date revalues open documents and foreign-currency banks and reverses itself the next day.
* **Bank reconciliation** – bank statements with their lines, **Match automatically** (same amount, ± 7 days, reference), bank charges and interest booked from the line, Reconciled; the bank reconciliation report.
* **Corporate tax** – each account has its treatment (deductible, entertainment 50 %, not deductible, exempt income, the tax itself); the computation: accounting profit → adjustments → taxable income → 0 % up to AED 375,000, 9 % above; small business relief when elected (revenue up to AED 3 million, tax periods ending by 31 Dec 2029); qualifying free-zone person setting; **Book the tax**.
* **E-invoicing** – with "E-invoicing" on, a posted customer invoice gets the type (380 invoice, 381 credit note), a UUID and the PINT AE UBL file for the accredited service provider (the company's ASP signs and transmits; ZEO does not send to the FTA).
* **The other apps** – Payroll, Inventory, Property … keep sending their journals to the accounting outbox; Journals › ZEO › **Post the journals of the other apps** posts them into these books (departments become cost centres). The stock journals of Inventory post to the same codes

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 194. Sales (1.77.0) › 194.1 How it works
sections.text:
* **One record from quotation to order** (as Odoo): a quotation (SQ-…) is sent, then **Confirm** makes it the sales order (SO-…). Copy, Lost (with the reason), Cancel / close what is left.
* **Prices** – each line takes the price of the order's price book (or the customer's, or the default one; fixed prices with quantity breaks or a % on the list price – the price books shared with CRM), else the item's list price; then the best **price rule** (by item, category or every item; for a customer; from a quantity; between dates; discount %, special price or buy X get Y – the lowest priority number wins). The user's own price or discount is kept. VAT code per line (Accounting's codes). Cost from Inventory (or the item cost) → margin per order.
* **Credit control** (set-up: off, warn, hold) – the customer's open balance in Accounting plus the orders not invoiced plus this order against the credit limit, and an invoice overdue more than the set-up days; a blocked customer or one on credit hold is refused. "Hold" puts the order **On credit hold** until the sales manager **releases** it.
* **Approvals** – a discount above the set-up %, an order above the set-up amount or a price below the item's minimum price waits for the sales manager (**Waiting for approval**).
* **Deliver** – all that is left or by line; the stocked items through an Inventory delivery (stock and cost of sales journals there), services without stock; **Backorders** report.
* **Invoice** (Accounting must be on) – by what was delivered (default) or by what was ordered (per order: services, advance billing); a **down payment** as a % of the order (to "Customer deposits and advances" 2400), deducted on the final invoice; the invoices are posted Accounting documents (source "sales").
* **Returns** – from the order:

* **Purchase requests** (feature) – a department asks for items (date needed, for which department or project, warehouse); Submit, the buyer approves or rejects; then **Make purchase orders** (one order per supplier: the cheapest valid supplier price of each item, else the item's preferred supplier) or **Ask suppliers for quotes**. **New request from the reorder list** turns Inventory's items below their reorder point into one approved request.
* **Requests for quotation** (feature) – the same items to several suppliers (by default those with a price for the items); enter each supplier's quote (price per line, delivery days, validity); the record shows the comparison line by line with the best price, and the quotes by total; **Award** (the chosen quote, or the lowest total) makes the purchase order draft and updates the supplier's price list. Optional rule: orders above the approval amount need a number of quotes.
* **Purchase orders** – the price of each line from the supplier's price list (the lowest valid price from the quantity), else the item's last purchase price or cost; VAT code per line (Accounting's purchase codes: SR-P, RC, IM …; reverse charge and imports carry no VAT on the order). **Submit**: below the approval amount it is approved at once; above it waits for the purchase manager, above the second amount also for the finance manager (Accounting's finance manager), each once and in order; **Send back** returns it to draft. A blocked supplier is refused.
* **Receive** – all that is left or by line, with the supplier's delivery note; stocked items through an Inventory goods receipt at the order price (stock value and goods-received-not-invoiced there), services without stock; receiving more than ordered is refused unless the set-up allows a %. Every screen has the common functions of the kit apps (list, search, filters, export, saved views, record with history, files, notes, print, confirm windows, Manufacturing home, My work, report centre, Features with presets, roles, branches, Arabic).

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 196. Manufacturing (1.79.0) › 196.1 How it works
sections.text:
* **Bills of materials** – what one batch of an item is made of: components with a scrap % and, with the feature, operations on work centres (set-up minutes per order, run minutes per unit). One default bill per item; **New version** copies it. **Roll up the cost**: components at their Inventory cost (a made component without stock: its own bill), plus labour, machine and overhead of the operations (the work centre's rates per hour and efficiency) → cost per unit.
* **Production orders** – the item, the quantity, the bill (the default one), the warehouse. **Release** copies the materials (with scrap) and the operations to the order, sets the planned cost per unit and warns of components short in the warehouse.
* **Issue materials** – all that is left or by line: an Inventory consumption document with the reason *Production – materials issued*, whose account role is work in progress (1450, from the production account set): Dr WIP, Cr inventory.
* **Report time** – minutes per operation (empty: the planned minutes): labour, machine and overhead absorbed – an Accounting entry Dr WIP, Cr *Production labour and overhead absorbed* (5990, set-up).
* **Report output** – the quantity made and scrapped; with **backflush** (set-up, default on) the materials for what is reported are taken first. The output goes to stock at the planned cost (Inventory adjustment, reason *Production – output to stock*: Dr inventory, Cr WIP). Producing more than ordered is refused unless the set-up allows a %.
* **Close** – what is left in work in progress for the order (materials + time − output) goes to *Production variances* (5900, set-up): unfavourable when more was used or scrapped, favourable when less. WIP for the order is then zero.
* **Make to order** (feature) – a confirmed Sales order becom

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 197. Large uploads and long reports (1.79.1)
sections.text: Version 1.79.1 = 1.79.0 + fixes for large data and one way of importing everywhere. Before this version, a list upload of more than about 1,000 rows or a report of more than about 1,000 pages kept the screen waiting until the browser or the web server gave up ("hanging"); the lists of the newer apps (Inventory, Accounting, Sales, Purchase, Manufacturing …) could not be imported at all. No migration.

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 197. Large uploads and long reports (1.79.1) › 197.1 What changed
sections.text:
* **List imports in the background** – an import of more than 200 rows (employees, leave, assets, any list with Import) is sent in pieces and runs in the background: the window shows "Checking 1,240 of 5,000 rows" / "Importing …" with a bar, **Stop** and **Continue** (it carries on from the last row done, also after a server restart), and a notice ("Import finished") when done. Only rows with a problem are kept for the window; **Download all N rows to fix (Excel)** gives them back to correct and import again. One import is one Undo, as before. At most 1,000,000 rows per import.
* **Faster employee import** – the rights and the leave-type facts are read once per import, not once per row: about 0.25 s a row on check and save (was 0.5–0.7 s).
* **Punch import** – more than 1,000 lines run in the background the same way (a 500,000-line check took 6.7 min).
* **Long reports on screen** – more than 2,000 rows: the screen shows 100 rows a page with search and sort. More than 20,000 rows: the rows stay on the server (a temporary file kept one day) and the screen asks for one page at a time; **Excel / CSV** of every row is made in the background and downloaded when ready (an Excel sheet holds at most 1,048,575 rows – CSV beyond that).
* **PDF of a long report** – more than 800 rows: made in the background in parts of 400 rows, joined into one file with "Page x of y" through the whole report; the window shows rows and pages done, and a notice ("PDF ready") opens the file. At most 100,000 rows per PDF; e-mailing a report of more than 20,000 rows is refused (download it instead).
* **Test before you import – every upload** – the list Import and every screen with its own upload (monthly inputs, opening balances, salary history, recoveries, pay splits, month roster, identity details,
