sections.text:
* **A long report never times out** – a report run on the report screen is prepared in a background thread of the server; the screen waits for it up to 20 seconds (`ZEO_REPORT_WAIT_SECONDS`), so a short report opens as before. A longer one – the daily attendance of 11,000 employees for three months took 112 s, near the 300 s a request may take – goes on in the background: the screen shows "Preparing the report: Attendance (daily)" and opens the report when it is ready; when it took longer than the wait, the notice "Report ready" in the Inbox opens it again (without preparing it again). PDF, Excel and the dashboards are not changed.
* **Test on the leave opening-balance import** – Leave › Leave balances › Import has **Test**: green, or red with each problem by the **line of the file** ("Line 5 – Employee code: no employee "NOSUCH777"", "Line 6 – Days: "abc" is not a number") and **Download the rows to fix (Excel)**; Import saves the correct rows and lists the others, as before.

* **Long lists open instead of freezing** – a list of thousands of rows (Leave balances of 1,000 employees: 20,268 rows) froze the browser tab and then crashed it. The shared list tools (search, filters, columns, record links) read every row, then set the status colours (a write between two reads made the browser lay out the whole table again for each row), read each cell's text once for the column formats, and find a row's record through an index of the loaded records (before: every row was compared with every record)

sections.text:
* **Every line in the Accounting reports** – the General ledger and the Journal register showed only the **first 20,000 lines** of the period, without saying so (a busy year has a million). They now show every line: read from the database as values, a chunk at a time, the opening of every account in one query. A general ledger of 1,028,937 rows (1,028,918 lines + an opening line per account) is ready in about 30 seconds – prepared in the background (1.79.2) and read a page at a time with search and sort over every line. The VAT audit file (400,000 VAT lines) the same way; VAT 201 is added up by the database per box.

It is built from values, not one object per movement (with a million movements the 1.79.2 code ran out of memory at 4.4 GB; now 22 s and 1.6 GB). The **stock movement summary** no longer builds the whole ledger only to add it up – the database adds up the opening, in, out and closing per item. **Stock ageing** reads the cost layers as values (the applications only of transfers); **KPIs** and the **integrity check** are added up / compared by the database (before: a list of every move id in one query).
* **Every record in the register reports** – the reports of each app list ("Invoices and bills", "Journal entries", "Stock documents" … and the HSE registers) stopped at **5,000 records** without saying so; they now have every record (the linked records read with the list).

sections.text:
##### 1. Posting into a closed year (like Sage 300 "Allow posting to prior years")
- Turn it on in Accounting setup › Settings › **Allow posting to closed years**.
- Once it is on, the **finance manager** can post a journal entry, reversal or corporate tax entry into a closed year. Invoices, bills, payments and other apps still can't post there.
- ZEO then posts a year-end adjustment for that entry on the last day of the closed year. The adjustment moves the entry's income and expense into **Retained earnings** straight away.
- That year's figures, the next year's opening balances and the balance sheet all stay correct, and there's no need to close the year again.
- When the option is off, a closed year takes no postings. The error message tells the user how to switch the option on or reopen the year.

##### 2. Reopen the year
- On a closed year, choose Financial years › **Reopen the year**. It is for the finance manager only and asks for a reason.
- It reverses the year-end entry and the retained-earnings adjustments, and opens the periods again.
- You can only reopen the latest closed year.
- Close the year again once the adjustments are in.

##### 3. Financial year start date (like Sage 200 Evolution)
- In Accounting setup there is a new **Financial year starts (day of the month)** setting, next to the start month. For example, month 3 and day 26 gives years running from 26 March to 25 March, with periods from the 26th to the 25th.
- A year can be created with any start and end date, up to 18 months long, as long as it doesn't overlap another year. Its periods are created automatically.
- **Period end dates can be edited.** When you move a period's end, the next period's start moves with it.
- Periods that don't start on the 1st are labelled by their dates, for examp

sections.section: 4. make the copies (each company keeps exactly the rights it had before the upgrade) › 200. Three 1.79.2 patches in one release (1.79.4) › 200.2 What changed – B. Year end and document capture › How it works
sections.text:
1. **The document goes in.**
   - Accepted files: PDF (tables kept as rows), scans and photos (OCR), Excel, CSV, Word, e-mail (.eml) and text.
   - You can also paste the e-mail text.
2. **ZEO reads it.**
   - With **Settings › AI settings › documents** on, the company's AI reads it. That covers free-form e-mails, abbreviations, scans and photos.
   - Otherwise the built-in reader is used, which handles tables, lists, Excel and Word.
   - Bank account (IBAN) and card numbers are masked before anything is sent to the AI.
3. **ZEO matches it.** It works in this order:
   1. What you taught it before.
   2. The supplier's own item codes (from the supplier price list), then SKU, barcode and part number.
   3. For the customer or supplier: TRN, e-mail (including the company's e-mail domain) and phone.
   4. Names. A different size counts against a match, so "2 ton" is not matched to "2.5 ton" and 1/2" is not matched to 3/8".

   With the AI on, unsure lines are also sent to the AI to choose from ZEO's own candidates (only item codes and names are sent).
4. **You review it.** The original document is shown beside the result. Each line is marked **Matched**, **Check** or **Not found**, and comes with:
   - a warning when its price differs from the price list or the supplier's prices
   - a warning when its unit differs from the item's unit
   - a check that the line totals agree with the document's total

   You can pick another item, change the quantity or price, leave a line out, or add a new customer or supplier.
5. **You create it.** ZEO uses each app's own numbering, defaults, VAT and rules.
   - When you correct a match, ZEO remembers it for that customer or supplier, so the next document matches it by itself.

sections.text:
**Purchase › Setup › Upload a supplier price list** (also on the "Read a document" screen):

- **What you can upload:** the supplier's list as Excel, CSV, PDF or a photo, or pasted from an e-mail.
- **What ZEO reads:**
  - the supplier, matched by TRN, e-mail or name
  - each item, matched first by the supplier's own codes, then by codes and names (with match %, pictures, search, match by photo or a new item, as in 1.79.5)
  - the price and discount
  - price breaks (the "MOQ / from quantity" column)
  - the validity: prices valid from … to …
  - the currency and the lead time
- **What the review screen shows:** next to every line, the current price and the change in %, for example "now 2,580.00 → -3.5 %".
- **Update the supplier's price list:**
  - **New price:** a new row.
  - **Changed price:** the current row ends the day before the new price starts, and a new row starts. The old price stays as history.
  - **Same price:** the supplier's code, lead time and validity are refreshed.
  - **Result:** a table of the changed prices (old → new, %), and a link to the supplier's prices.
- **Who can use it:** the Purchase manager (the price list is master data), with the Supplier prices feature on.

sections.section: ZEO HRMS – installing from scratch (package 1.79.5)
ZEO HRMS – installing from scratch (package 1.79.5) › 1. Server
sections.text:
Tested with:
- Ubuntu 22.04 / 24.04
- Python 3.12 or 3.13
- PostgreSQL 14–16
- Redis 6–7
- Node.js 18–22 (only to build the frontend)
- nginx

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y python3-venv python3-dev build-essential libpq-dev postgresql redis-server nginx
```

sections.section: ZEO HRMS – installing from scratch (package 1.79.5) › 2. Database
sections.text:
```bash
sudo -u postgres psql -c "CREATE USER zeo_user WITH PASSWORD 'choose-a-strong-password';"
sudo -u postgres psql -c "CREATE DATABASE zeo OWNER zeo_user;"
```
Each company gets its own schema in this database. The database user must own the database, because it creates the schemas.

sections.section: ZEO HRMS – installing from scratch (package 1.79.5) › 3. Backend
sections.text:
```bash
sudo mkdir -p /opt/zeo && sudo chown $USER /opt/zeo
cp -r zeo-hrms /opt/zeo/
cd /opt/zeo/zeo-hrms
python3 -m venv /opt/zeo/venv
/opt/zeo/venv/bin/pip install --upgrade pip
/opt/zeo/venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env
nano .env
```

What to set in `.env`:
- `ZEO_SECRET_KEY`: make one with `python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(50))"`.
- `ZEO_DB_*`: the database from step 2.
- `ZEO_ALLOWED_HOSTS`: the server's host name or IP.
- `ZEO_CORS_ORIGINS`: the address users open the app from, e.g. `https://hr.example.com`.
- `ZEO_EMAIL_*`: the company mail account. Leave it empty to write e-mails to the log while testing.
- `ZEO_DEBUG`: keep it `false` on a server.
- `ZEO_APP_URL`: the address users open, e.g. `https://hr.example.com` (links in e-mails, password links).
- `ZEO_HTTPS`: `true` once the server has a certificate (secure cookies, HSTS); `false` for a plain http test install.
- `ZEO_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`: the same https address (defaults to `ZEO_APP_URL`).

Keep `.env` private: `chmod 600 .env`. It is the only place passwords live.

Face punching needs the large optional packages listed at the end of `requirements.txt`. Install them only if you use face attendance.

sections.section: ZEO HRMS – installing from scratch (package 1.79.5) › 5. Run the backend
sections.text:
Copy the examples from `deploy/` and adjust the paths and user:
- `zeo-gunicorn.service` runs the API on 127.0.0.1:8000;
- `zeo-celery.service` and `zeo-celery-beat.service` run the scheduled jobs. These include leave accrual and escalations, attendance (absent marking, missing punches), shift reminders, document and probation reminders, and asset reminders.

```bash
sudo cp deploy/zeo-*.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now zeo-gunicorn zeo-celery zeo-celery-beat
```

sections.section: ZEO HRMS – installing from scratch (package 1.79.5) › 6. Frontend
sections.text:
Choose one:

- **Ready-built:** copy `frontend-build/` to `/var/www/zeo/`.
- **Build it yourself:**
  ```bash
  cd zeo-frontend/hrms-project
  npm install
  npx ng build
  ```
  Then copy `dist/hrms-project/browser/` to `/var/www/zeo/`.

**Never use `ng serve` on a server** – it is a developer tool: slow, shows the source paths and is not secure. Always serve the built files with nginx (step 7).

**API address:** edit `/var/www/zeo/assets/env.js`. No rebuild is needed.
- `window.ZEO_API_URL = ''` (automatic) uses `http://localhost:8000` when the app is opened on localhost. On any other host it uses the same host name as the page, so it works when nginx serves the app and the API on one name (step 7).
- To use a separate API host, set it, e.g. `window.ZEO_API_URL = 'https://api.yourcompany.com';`.

sections.section: ZEO HRMS – installing from scratch (package 1.79.5) › 7. nginx
sections.text:
Use `deploy/nginx-zeo.conf`. It does the following:
- serves the app;
- passes the API paths to gunicorn;
- passes `/iclock/` to gunicorn, for ZKTeco attendance devices pushing punches (set the device's server address to this host);
- serves `/media/`.

```bash
sudo cp deploy/nginx-zeo.conf /etc/nginx/sites-available/zeo
sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/zeo /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/zeo
sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
```

Add HTTPS with `sudo certbot --nginx -d hr.yourcompany.com`. Then put `https://hr.yourcompany.com` in `ZEO_CORS_ORIGINS`.

sections.section: ZEO HRMS – installing from scratch (package 1.79.5) › 8. First login and setup in the app
sections.text:
1. Open the app and log in with the administrator's e-mail address and password, then pick the company.
2. Settings:
   - Company: logo, address, Employer unique ID (WPS), bank routing code.
   - Branches: add the other branches.
   - E-mail configuration: the company's own mail account, if any.
3. Employees → Setup:
   - departments, designations, categories;
   - Employee code numbering;
   - Form designer.
4. Organisation → Settings: switch on the structures you use (locations, sections, cost centres, grades and so on).
   Settings → **Languages**: switch on Arabic if the company wants it and choose the default language (each user can pick their own in the top bar).
   Settings → **Country settings**: check the country pack (captions such as Emirates ID / Iqama, which fields and reports show, currency, gratuity rules). UAE companies need no change.
5. Settings → User groups and Branch permissions: give HR users their branches. HR users without a branch see empty lists.
6. Leave → Leave policies: check the UAE setup and assign the categories.
7. Payroll → Salary components:
   - Add **Leave Encashment** (`leave_encashment_amount`), **Expense Reimbursement** (`expense_reimbursement_amount`) and **Asset recovery** (`asset_recovery_amount`).
   - Run `check_salary_formulas --fix`.
8. Time & Attendance → Attendance rules: create the company rule and exempt staff who do not punch, before the first night. Otherwise they are marked absent.
9. Shift Planner → Shift master, then the first roster.
10. Employees → Self-service settings: what employees may change, letter templates, complaint officers.
11. Import employees (Employees → Import), then identity details (Employees → Import identity details).

sections.section: ZEO HRMS – installing from scratch (package 1.79.5) › 9. Backups

sections.section: ZEO HRMS – installing from scratch (package 1.79.5) › 10. Updating later
sections.text:
1. Copy the new files over `/opt/zeo/zeo-hrms` (keep `.env` and `media/`).
2. Run `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
3. Run `python manage.py migrate_schemas`.
4. Restart gunicorn, the Celery worker and beat.
5. Replace the frontend files, keeping your `assets/env.js`.

Each update's README lists any extra one-time steps. From 1.67.19 or older to 1.67.20: see `DEVELOPER-SETUP-1.79.5.md`.

sections.section: ZEO HRMS – installing from scratch (package 1.79.5) › Known limits
sections.text:
The list of open points is at the end of `README-UPDATE.md`. In short:
- Uploaded files under `/media/` need a login since 1.56.1 (nginx asks Django, see `deploy/nginx-zeo.conf`); company logos stay public.
- New self-service logins get an e-mail link to choose their own password when `ZEO_APP_URL` is set (1.56.0); otherwise a random temporary password that must be changed at the first login.
- Leave follows the leave policies of each company; gratuity / end of service follows the country rule set; the statutory schemes (GPSSA, GOSI, PASI, SIO, PIFSS, EPF / ESI …) are calculated since 1.31.0 – verify the rates with your adviser.

sections.section: ZEO Projects – add-on package (v1.15.0, 10 October 2026)
sections.text:
> **v1.15.0** adds:
> * **Plan templates** per product / project type (Delivery → Plan templates): phases, tasks, working-day timing, hours,
>   role, milestones (% of value), customer approval. Pick one on *New project* (map roles to people) or *Apply plan
>   template* later; *Save as template* from any project. The plan stays editable (add / edit / delete tasks, assign
>   people and hours) and exports to **Excel and PDF**, with a timeline column.
>   A default template **"IT implementation – System study to Go-live"** (32 tasks + 8 sub-tasks, 9 phases, 638 h, ~12 weeks,
>   6 customer sign-off milestones = 100 %) is created by `zeoprojects_setup` and can be added any time with
>   *+ Add the default template* on the Plan templates page.
> * **Expected dates required**: a project needs its expected start and end (the end can come from the template) and
>   every task and sub-task its expected start and end; ZEO records the **actual start / end** when a task is started /
>   completed and shows both in the plan and the export.
> * **Sub-tasks**: *+ Sub* on any main task (one level); a sub-task must lie within its main task's dates, a main task
>   cannot be completed while a sub-task is open, and templates carry sub-tasks (the *Sub* column).
> * **Task attachments**: 📎 on every task and sub-task – upload several files (20 MB each) with a note, download,
>   remove (who uploaded it or the project manager). API: `tasks/<id>/files/`, `task-files/<id>/`.
> * **Channels** WhatsApp, walk-in, Teams / video call and live chat on tickets, and a **WhatsApp button** on the ticket
>   (opens wa.me with a prepared message – free, no WhatsApp API).
> * **Work approval**: tickets covered by an AMC are assigned straight away; tickets **not covered** wait for a support
>   manager's a

sections.text:
pproval (and assignment) before work starts; time beyond **1 hour** per ticket (Setup → General) needs
>   an approval – the engineer clicks *Ask for more time*, the manager approves the hours. Managers are not limited.
> * **Notifications**: customer acknowledgement on every new ticket, the engineer and the customer's account manager are
>   told; a ticket not solved in time now also goes to the engineer (e-mail + My To-do), then team lead and managers;
>   **overdue project tasks** e-mail the people on the task and the project managers (daily job, repeated weekly) and
>   show on *My work*. Settings at three levels: **company** (Setup → Notifications), **customer** (customer page) and
>   **user** (My work → My notifications), e-mail and To-do separately.
> * **Work history report** (Reports → History): all time on AMC support, chargeable support and project tasks for a
>   customer, AMC contract or project and period, plus tickets and task status – Excel / CSV / PDF, a full PDF / Excel,
>   and **Send by e-mail** to the customer with both files attached.
>
> New fields and tables → run `makemigrations ZeoProjects` and `migrate_schemas` again. No settings.py change.

> **v1.14.1** added Projects → Reports, dashboard "Full report ›" links, the cost-budget meter and the weekly summary e-mail.

**Projects** turns ZEO into an IT service management system: customers and contacts, support tickets with SLA and
escalation, AMC contracts (coverage, hours, billing, renewals), development requests with a three-step approval,
project delivery (milestones / UAT sign-off, change requests, risks and issues, profitability), a management
dashboard, **reports with Excel / PDF export** and a **customer portal**.

It is built as **new code only**, so it can be merged into your latest ZEO

sections.section: ZEO Projects – add-on package (v1.15.0, 10 October 2026) › 1. Merge – backend
sections.text:
1. Copy `backend/ZeoProjects/` into the project folder (next to `ProjectControl/`).
2. `zeo/settings.py`
   - `TENANT_APPS` – add after `'SelfService',`:
     ```python
     'ZeoProjects',       # v1.14.0 Projects: customers, support tickets with SLA, AMC contracts, delivery, customer portal
     ```
   - `MIDDLEWARE` – add after `'Chatter.tracking.CurrentRequestMiddleware',`:
     ```python
     'ZeoProjects.middleware.PortalGuardMiddleware',  # v1.14.0 customer portal users may only use the portal API
     ```
   - `CELERY_BEAT_SCHEDULE` – add:
     ```python
     'zeoprojects-sla-check': {'task': 'ZeoProjects.tasks.sla_check', 'schedule': crontab(minute='*/15')},
     'zeoprojects-mailbox': {'task': 'ZeoProjects.tasks.check_mailboxes', 'schedule': crontab(minute='*/5')},
     'zeoprojects-daily': {'task': 'ZeoProjects.tasks.daily', 'schedule': crontab(hour=7, minute=35)},
     ```
3. `zeo/urls.py` – add:
   ```python
   path('zeo-projects/', include('ZeoProjects.urls')),          # v1.14.0 Projects
   ```
4. Tables (no migration files are shipped – same as the other apps):
   ```bash
   python manage.py makemigrations ZeoProjects
   python manage.py migrate_schemas
   ```
5. Defaults and role groups (safe to run again):
   ```bash
   python manage.py zeoprojects_setup --roles            # every company
   python manage.py zeoprojects_setup --schema <schema>  # one company, defaults only
   ```
   Creates the "Standard" SLA policy (the sample targets of the specification), issue categories, products, support
   teams and the role groups below.
6. Restart the API, the Celery worker and Celery beat.

Or apply `patches/zeo-projects-backend.patch` from the backend root (`git apply patches/zeo-projects-backend.patch`).

sections.section: ZEO Projects – add-on package (v1.15.0, 10 October 2026) › 3. What the users get › Tickets
sections.text:
- Channels: customer portal, employee helpdesk, e-mail (IMAP mailbox), entered by support, phone; `channel` also accepts web / api.
- Stages: New → Assigned → In Progress → Waiting for Customer / Waiting for Internal Team → Pending Development Approval →
  Under Development → Testing → Resolved → Closed → Reopened (illegal moves are refused; resolving needs resolution notes).
- Automatic: AMC contract and coverage (product covered? development excluded? hours used up? → chargeable), team by
  category / product, assignment to the least busy team member, SLA targets.
- SLA: response and resolution targets per priority and policy (contract → customer → company default). Business-hours
  targets count only the working days / hours of the settings and skip ZEO holiday calendars; 24/7 contracts count all
  hours. The clock pauses while the ticket waits for the customer.
- Every 15 minutes: breaches are marked and escalated (assignee → team lead → support managers, repeated every N
  minutes), critical tickets not assigned after 15 minutes go to the managers, customers who keep a ticket waiting are
  reminded, resolved tickets close after N days.
- Conversation with the customer plus **internal notes** (never shown in the portal), files, history, work logs
  (remote / onsite, chargeable, travel and other charges, approval), satisfaction rating.
- Notifications: e-mail (the company's active E-mail configuration) and items in **My To-do** (Chatter activities).

sections.section: ZEO Projects – add-on package (v1.15.0, 10 October 2026) › 3. What the users get › Development requests
sections.text:
Support engineer raises it from a ticket → **technical review** → **commercial approval** (chargeable only, quoted
amount) → **customer approval** (portal, or recorded by staff) → a **task is created** in the customer's project
(or in "Support development – <customer>") with planned hours → in development → testing → deployed → customer
confirms → the ticket is resolved.

sections.section: ZEO Projects – add-on package (v1.15.0, 10 October 2026) › 3. What the users get › AMC contracts
sections.text:
Number, customer, products covered, type, start / end, value, billing frequency (instalments are built automatically),
included hours (or unlimited) and onsite hours, SLA policy, support timing, exclusions, account manager, renewal
status, versions (each renewal is a new contract linked to the previous one). Hours used = approved and submitted
work logs that count against the AMC; remaining hours, revenue (value + chargeable work outside), cost (work logs at
salary-based cost rate), margin. Renewal reminders 90 / 60 / 30 / 0 days before expiry and every N days after
(configurable) as e-mail + To-do for the renewal owner.

sections.section: ZEO Projects – add-on package (v1.15.0, 10 October 2026) › 3. What the users get › Projects
sections.text:
Uses the existing ZEO projects and adds: number, customer, project type, billing method, contract / LPO reference,
scope, deliverables; tasks with phase, priority, acceptance criteria, reviewer, dependencies, sub-tasks, blockers,
progress and customer approval; milestones with dependencies, **customer acceptance in the portal (UAT sign-off)** and
invoicing; change requests (internal approval → customer approval → budget hours raised); risks and issues;
third-party costs; profitability (value + change requests, invoiced, employee cost from approved timesheets,
expenses, estimate to complete, expected margin) and health (on track / at risk / delayed).

sections.section: ZEO Projects – add-on package (v1.15.0, 10 October 2026) › 3. What the users get › Customer portal
sections.text:
- Address: `https://<your ZEO>/portal/login?c=<company schema>` (set it under Projects settings → Customer portal).
- Staff invite a contact from the customer page (**Invite to portal**); the login is the contact's e-mail and the
  password is shown once and e-mailed.
- Contacts see their own tickets (or all company tickets when "All company tickets" is set), raise tickets with files,
  reply, confirm or reopen, rate; see contracts with hours used / left, projects with progress and milestones,
  invoices, and – when "May approve" is ticked – approve milestones, change requests, development quotations and tasks.
- Portal users have no group rights. `PortalGuardMiddleware` blocks them from every API except the portal API, and
  the portal API only returns rows of their own customer.

sections.section: ZEO Projects – add-on package (v1.15.0, 10 October 2026) › 3. What the users get › Roles (`zeoprojects_setup --roles`)
sections.text:
| Group | Main rights |
|---|---|
| Projects – Support Manager | all tickets, assign / escalate / close, approve work logs, technical approval, SLA and team set-up |
| Projects – Support Engineer | tickets of own teams and own tickets, work logs, raise development requests |
| Projects – AMC Account Manager | customers, contacts, contracts, renewals, billing view |
| Projects – Project Manager | projects (ProjectManagement rights), project finance, milestones, change requests, risks |
| Projects – Developer | assigned tickets and project tasks |
| Projects – Finance | billing (record invoice numbers / payments), commercial approval, profitability |
| Projects – Management | dashboards and reports, change request approval (read-only otherwise) |
| System administrator | company admin – everything |
| Customer portal user | portal only (see above) |

sections.section: ZEO Projects – add-on package (v1.15.0, 10 October 2026) › 3. What the users get › Reports (Projects → Reports)
sections.text:
Each report has filters (period, customer, team, employee, status, group by), a totals row, sortable columns,
click-through to the ticket / contract / project behind a row, and Excel, CSV and PDF export. Rows follow the same
rights as the screens (an engineer sees the support reports for the tickets he may see; money columns need the
finance right).

| Group | Report |
|---|---|
| Support | Open tickets by engineer / team / customer / priority · Received vs resolved per week (with backlog) · Response and resolution times in working hours and clock time, SLA compliance · SLA breached tickets · Reopened tickets and customer rating per engineer |
| AMC | All contracts – value, billed, paid, outstanding, hours included / used / left, chargeable work, cost, margin · Contracts expiring in 30 / 60 / 90 days · Renewals won, lost and pending (renewal rate) |
| Projects | Project status – health, milestones, tasks, planned vs actual hours, cost budget used %, revenue, invoiced, margin · Overdue milestones · Pending tasks and overdue work (tasks + tickets) per employee |
| People | Utilisation – available, support, project and billable hours, open and overdue work · Work logs waiting for approval |

**Weekly summary e-mail** – every Monday with the daily job (no new scheduled job): open / critical / past-SLA tickets,
received vs resolved, SLA %, customer rating, AMC expiries and renewals, the past-SLA list and contracts ending soon.
Setup → *Weekly summary e-mail*: on/off and the addresses (empty = users with the support-manager or change-approval
right). Reports → *Weekly summary e-mail* shows a preview and has *Send now*.

sections.section: ZEO Projects – add-on package (v1.15.0, 10 October 2026) › 3. What the users get › E-mail to ticket
sections.text:
Projects settings → Support mailbox: IMAP server, user, password, folder. Unread mails become tickets (contact
matched by e-mail, customer by e-mail domain, team by the to-address = team e-mail alias); replies with the ticket
number in the subject are added to that ticket (and reopen / resume it); automatic replies are skipped.
No paid service is used.

---

`contacts/` (+ `<id>/portal/`), `tickets/` (+ `<id>/assign|stage|messages|worklogs|dev-request/`), `files/<id>/`,

sections.section: ZEO Projects – add-on package (v1.15.0, 10 October 2026) › 5. Check after deploying
sections.text:
- `zeoprojects_setup --roles` printed the groups; give users the groups in Settings → Permission groups.
- As a support manager: Projects → Customers → New customer with a contact → AMC contracts → New contract (activate).
- Tickets → New ticket for that customer: the AMC, "AMC covered", team, engineer and SLA times are filled in.
- Customer page → Invite to portal → open `/portal/login?c=<schema>` in a private window → sign in → raise a ticket.
- Reply as the engineer, add an internal note → the portal shows the reply, not the note.
- Raise a development request → approve technical, commercial, then in the portal → a task appears in the project.
- Dashboard shows the figures; the engineer does not see Dashboard / AMC / Billing in the menu.
- `celery -A zeo beat` lists the three new jobs.
- Projects → Reports: open each report, export one to Excel and PDF, click a row to open the ticket / contract / project.
- Reports → Weekly summary e-mail → Send now arrives at the managers' mailboxes.
- v1.15.0: a ticket for a product outside the AMC shows *Waiting for approval*; approve it as a support manager.
  Log more than 1 hour as an engineer → *Ask for more time* → approve. Create a project from a plan template and
  export the plan. Reports → Work history → Send by e-mail.

sections.section: ZEO Projects – add-on package (v1.15.0, 10 October 2026) › 6. Notes and limits
sections.text:
- **Invoices** are not created by ZEO (there is no accounting module): finance records the invoice number, date and
  payment of AMC instalments and milestones. Connect to accounting later.
- **WhatsApp** tickets are not included (needs the paid WhatsApp Business API); the `api` channel is ready for it.
- Ticket files are downloaded through the API with a login check. Files under `/media/` are still served by the web
  server – keep `/media/` behind authentication (same note as earlier updates).
- The mailbox password is stored in the database like the company e-mail configuration.
- Reports are calculated live from the data; on very large companies narrow the period or filter by customer.
- Tested on a local copy: 96 end-to-end API checks, all 13 reports for every role (rights, portal lock-down, SLA business-hours clock, approvals,
  coverage, renewals, e-mail threading) and a full `ng build` without errors or warnings.

sections.section: README-HSE.md
sections.text: > **Merged into ZEO 1.21.0.** This is the README of the add-on as received. Its installation steps are already done in ZEO 1.21.0 – follow README.md, Deploy step 26, instead. Activation and the industry of the app are now in **Settings → Apps**.

sections.section: ZEO HSE v1.17.0: all 15 blueprint modules, industry packs and links with the other ZEO apps
sections.text:
HSE is a new ZEO module (Django app `ZeoHSE`, Angular folder `zeo-hse`). It covers all 15 modules of the HSE/EHS blueprint, plus central CAPA, document control and training/competency. It also includes four industry template packs. **From v1.17.0, HSE asks for its industry when it is activated**: the company's **Industry type** is the default, and the HSE manager can keep it or change it for HSE only.

> Pack content (permits, forms, checklists, approval matrices, terminology, hazards, KPIs, exposure limits) is a starting point only. An HSE manager must review it against the company's real hazards, operating procedures and the legal requirements that apply. Until then, permit types and checklists cannot be used.

sections.section: ZEO HSE v1.17.0: all 15 blueprint modules, industry packs and links with the other ZEO apps › What is included
sections.text:
| # | Blueprint module | Where in ZEO (HSE menu) | Main rules enforced |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Incident management | Safety operations › Incidents | Every employee reports. A high-potential event (potential severity 4–5) is investigated even without injury. Before closing you need a root cause, verified actions and the authority reference. Closure is approved through the approval matrix. A closed record can only be corrected with a logged reason. Health details are restricted. |
| 2 | Management of change | Assurance › Management of change | Flow: draft → screening → impact assessment (6 areas) → approval (matrix by permanent/temporary/emergency) → pre-start verification → implementation → post-change review → closed. Medium or high impact needs an approved HIRA/JSA. New hazards flag the risk assessment for review. |
| 3 | Occupational health | Health › Occupational health | Surveillance schedule with automatic next periodic check. Clinical findings are visible only to occupational health and the HSE manager. A line manager sees only the fitness outcome and restrictions of their own staff. |
| 4 | Audit management | Assurance › Audits | Conflict-of-interest check. Checklist results are compliant / not compliant / observation / N/A. Findings are created automatically and repeat findings are flagged. The report is approved by someone other than the auditor. A CAPA is raised for each finding. The audit cannot close until the actions are verified. PDF report. |
| 5 | Quality management | Assurance › Quality nonconformities | Flow: containment → disposition approved by the quality manager (not the reporter) → root cause → actions → re-inspection → closure. |
| 6 | Permit to work | Safety operations › Permits | A permit is issued only when every prerequisite is met: reviewe

sections.section: ZEO HSE v1.17.0: all 15 blueprint modules, industry packs and links with the other ZEO apps › What is included
sections.text:
d type, approved risk assessment (not under review), method statement, critical checklist items, fresh gas test within limits, isolations verified by a second person, approved contractor with valid documents, valid crew competencies, team briefed, and validity within the maximum. SIMOPS conflicts block submission. A failed gas test suspends the permit. Hand-back checks are required to close. Printed copies carry a QR code. |
| 7 | Business performance | Performance › KPIs, Management reviews | TRIR, LTIFR, near misses, audit completion, action closure, training compliance and more are calculated monthly. The rate multiplier is configurable. Deviations notify the KPI owner. A management review takes a snapshot of the inputs and records decisions and actions. |
| 8 | Risk assessment | Safety operations › Risk assessments | 5×5 matrix with configurable bands. Extreme residual risk is blocked. Approval follows the matrix by band, and you cannot approve your own assessment. A risk assessment is reviewed after an incident or change. Revisions supersede the old version and open permits move to the new one. |
| 9 | Ergonomics | Health › Ergonomics | Any assessment method (REBA, RULA, NIOSH, MAC…). Control actions. Reassessment with effectiveness. |
| 10 | Environmental | Environment › monitoring, aspects, waste | Aspect significance is calculated. A reading outside its limit raises an alert and an action automatically. Waste transfer needs an approved carrier, and hazardous waste also needs a manifest and permit number. Disposal needs evidence. |
| 11 | Chemicals and SDS | Environment › Chemicals and SDS | Approval is blocked while documentation is missing or the SDS is more than 5 years old. Incompatible storage is flagged. A new SDS revision sends the chemical back to review.

sections.section: ZEO HSE v1.17.0: all 15 blueprint modules, industry packs and links with the other ZEO apps › What is included
sections.text:
Everyone can read approved chemicals for emergency information. |
| 12 | Behaviour-based safety | Safety operations › BBS observations | Safe and at-risk behaviour, categories, confidential reporting. A high-risk observation alerts the HSE manager and can be escalated to an incident. Trends are by category and place, never by person. |
| 13 | Claims | Actions › Claims | Restricted to the claims officer, the HSE manager and senior management. Records the insurer decision. Settlement needs internal approval. A claim cannot close unreconciled. |
| 14 | Industrial hygiene | Health › Industrial hygiene, Exposure limits | Limits are version-controlled by jurisdiction. Calibration must be within 12 months. An exceedance raises an action and notifies occupational health, with no medical conclusion drawn. A retest date is set. |
| 15 | Compliance | Assurance › Compliance register | Obligations with owner and reviewer. An assessment needs evidence and is approved by the reviewer (not the assessor). A gap raises a CAPA. An obligation more than 7 days overdue escalates to the owner's line manager, the site manager and the HSE manager. |
| – | Central CAPA | Actions › Corrective actions | One register for all sources. The owner completes with evidence and someone else verifies effectiveness, or the action is reopened. Reassignment and due-date changes need a reason. Overdue actions are escalated. |
| – | Document control | My safety › Documents | Flow: draft → review → approval (not the author) → published → revision (supersedes the old one). Staff acknowledgement is recorded. |
| – | Training and competency | Shared registers | Expiry is calculated from the validity period. An expired or missing competency blocks permit issue, or only warns if you configure it that way. |

sections.section: ZEO HSE v1.17.0: all 15 blueprint modules, industry packs and links with the other ZEO apps › What is included › Industry packs (chosen when HSE is activated)
sections.text:
| Company "Industry type" (the default) | HSE pack suggested |
|---|---|
| Construction and engineering (`CON`, new) | Excavation, lifting and confined-space permits; method statement; scaffold, excavation, lifting-gear and daily site inspections; subcontractor pre-qualification; toolbox talks; rigger, crane and scaffold competencies; site audit |
| Manufacturing (`MFG`) | LOTO and chemical-handling permits; guarding, forklift, pressure-system, chemical-store, hygiene and environmental inspections; quality NC form; plant audit; exposure-limit samples |
| Healthcare (`HC`) | ICRA and medical-gas permits; sharps/waste, infection-control and hazardous-drug inspections; code-red drill; restricted health categories (sharps, blood and body fluid); BLS, IPC and sharps competencies |
| Oil and gas (`OG`, new) | Hot, cold, confined-space-entry, isolation-certificate and radiography permits with gas limits and SIMOPS rules; SIMOPS review; gas detection; H₂S and spill drills; H₂S and BOSIET competencies; PTW audit |
| Any other industry | General pack: risk matrix, approval matrices, general/hot-work/height/electrical permits, workplace inspection, evacuation drill, KPIs, ISO 45001-structured audit |

**Activation (v1.17.0)**

1. Until HSE is activated, every HSE page opens **Activate HSE**. HSE installs nothing when a company is created.
2. The screen shows the company industry from the company master and the HSE pack it suggests, then asks: **"Do you want to change the industry for HSE?"**
   - **No:** HSE is activated with the company industry's pack.
   - **Yes, change it:** the HSE manager picks another pack. This is for HSE only; the company master is not changed.
3. Only the HSE manager or a company administrator can activate HSE. Other users see "HSE is not activated yet".

How it is built:

- New file `ZeoHSE/links.py`.
- A link is on when the other app is in `INSTALLED_APPS`, its tables exist in the company schema, and the HSE manager has not switched it off.
- HSE stores other apps' records as plain ids (`project_id`, `asset_id`, `course_id` …), never as foreign keys. HSE tables and migrations therefore never depend on another app.
- Every call into another app is guarded. A failure there is logged and never blocks the HSE record, or the other app's record.
- Signals react at once (certificate, leave, rejoining, offer, transfer, resignation, complaint). The daily HSE job (07:40) also catches anything saved by bulk updates or imports. **Setup › Links › Save and bring in records now** runs it on demand.
- Privacy is kept the same way as in HSE:
  - leave details on an incident are shown to HSE staff only;
  - the project tab never shows injured names, treatment or health details;
  - HSE costs are for the HSE manager, claims officer and senior management.

sections.section: ZEO HSE v1.17.0: all 15 blueprint modules, industry packs and links with the other ZEO apps › Ask ZEO AI for HSE (v1.16.1)
sections.text:
Ask ZEO AI (the button in the top bar) now answers HSE questions as well as HR ones. Examples:

- "How is our HSE performance this month?" gives incidents, near misses, TRIR and LTIFR (with the multiplier and hours used), live permits and overdue actions.
- "Which corrective actions are overdue?" and "Which permits are live right now?" give a table with a link to each record.
- "How many incidents by category this year?" gives counts grouped by category.
- "What is waiting for me in HSE?" lists my approvals, actions to do and verify, permits, investigations and documents to read.

How it works:

- New file `ZeoHSE/ask.py` holds three tools: `hse_summary`, `hse_query` (any of the 25 HSE registers: filter, group, sort) and `hse_my_work`.
- `patches/hse-ask-zeo-ai.patch` connects them to `DashboardManagement/assistant.py`. It adds the tools for the AI, HSE keywords for basic mode, HSE suggestions and HSE answering rules in the system prompt.
- Every tool runs **as the asking user**, with the same rights as the HSE screens:
  - Employees get only their own records.
  - Company figures are for HSE staff and senior management only.
  - Clinical findings and claims stay hidden from anyone without the right.
  - Only the returned rows (max 100, long texts cut) are sent to the AI provider.

Modes:

- **Without** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (basic mode, no cost), simple HSE questions are answered from keywords: summary, overdue actions, live/suspended permits, incidents, near misses, high-potential events, audits, chemicals, waste, compliance, observations and more.
- **With** the key, full natural-language questions work across all HSE registers.

Install:

1. Copy `ZeoHSE` again (it now includes `ask.py`).
2. Run `git apply --ignore-whitespace patches/hse-ask-zeo-ai.patch`.
3. Restart

sections.text:
Three separate apps, sold and installed on their own. When two or all three are installed **and activated** in a company,
they connect automatically. Each app is set up for its industry at activation (company master industry by default,
the manager is asked whether to change it; *General* = no industry-specific setup).

| App | What it does | Linked with |
|---|---|---|
| **CRM** (`ZeoCRM`, `/main-sidebar/zeo-crm`) | Contacts (duplicate check), pipelines and stages, opportunities (list + board), activities, viewings, offers, listings; first-contact SLA, round-robin assignment, lost reasons, dashboard | Property: pick units, *Reserve the unit* from a deal, one contact per tenant/buyer, renewal opportunities, listing status follows the unit. Maintenance: *Send to Maintenance* |
| **Property** (`ZeoProperty`, `/main-sidebar/zeo-property`) | Buildings, units (status rules), owners, management agreements, tenants/buyers, reservations (expiry), leases (versions, rent schedule, deposit, post-dated cheques, renewal, notice, move-out), sale contracts (payment plan, handover checklist), **billing records** (invoice made in your accounting system – Excel export + invoice no. field), receipts with allocation, cheque life cycle (bounced → alerts), commissions with approval, deposit settlement, owner statements; **tenant / owner / buyer portals** | CRM: deals → reservations → leases / sales, renewal alerts open CRM renewals. Maintenance: move-in / move-out / unit-ready / snag inspections, portal requests, owner approval, recharges |
| **Maintenance** (`ZeoMaintenance`, `/main-sidebar/zeo-maintenance`) | Categories with response / fix times and who pays, locations, assets, vendors, work orders (assign → quotes → approval → work → close), cost lines, preventive plans (jobs made automat

sections.text:
ically), inspections with checklists | Property: work on units, tenant shown, owner approves above the agreement limit (owner portal), close → billing record to tenant or owner, inspection results → deposit deductions / unit back to *available* |

All three run on a shared engine, the **ZEO app kit** (`zeo/appkit/`): activation per app, industry packs (*to review* until a
manager confirms them; packs only ever **add**), roles as permission groups, a generic register API (list / create / change /
workflow actions / files / history / Excel export) and the links. A link works only when the other app is installed, migrated
and activated in that company; the other app's records are kept as plain ids (never foreign keys), so removing an app never
breaks the others. A manager can switch any link off in *Setup › Links with other apps*.

sections.section: ZEO mobile app (1.25.0) – build it and put it on Google Play
sections.text:
The ZEO app for Android is in this frontend project. It is the same Angular code as the web, packaged with **Capacitor 8**: the app opens the phone screens (`/m`) and uses the phone for fingerprint sign-in, push notifications, GPS, camera and files. The Android project is in `android/`; the app id is **`ae.adept.zeo`** (it can never change after the first upload – change it in `capacitor.config.ts` and `android/app/build.gradle` *before* that if Adept prefers another one).

What the app does: choose ZEO Cloud or a company server · sign in (password, code for office users) · fingerprint / face sign-in · company list · home with a one-tap check in / out (GPS and selfie when the company asks) · leave balance, request and withdraw leave · payslips as PDF · my requests · approvals for managers (approve / reject) · English and Arabic · open full ZEO.

The server must run ZEO **1.25.0 or later** (it answers `/mobile/api/info/`) and should be on **https**.

---

sections.section: ZEO mobile app (1.25.0) – build it and put it on Google Play › 1. Build the app › A. On GitHub (no Android Studio needed) – recommended
sections.text:
1. Put the frontend in a GitHub repository (the workflow is `.github/workflows/zeo-android.yml` at the root of `zeo-frontend`).
2. GitHub → **Actions** → **ZEO Android app** → **Run workflow** (version name `1.25.0`, version code `12500`).
3. After about 15 minutes: the run → **Artifacts** → `zeo-android-1.25.0.zip` with
   - `zeo-1.25.0-debug.apk` – install on a test phone (copy to the phone, open it, allow "install unknown apps");
   - `zeo-1.25.0-release.aab` – the file for Google Play (signed when the secrets below are set).
4. Secrets (repository → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions):

| Secret | What |
|---|---|
| `ZEO_KEYSTORE_BASE64` | the upload key file as base64 (step 2.3) |
| `ZEO_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `ZEO_KEY_ALIAS`, `ZEO_KEY_PASSWORD` | its passwords and alias |
| `GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON` | content of `google-services.json` from Firebase (push notifications, step 4) |
| `ZEO_CLOUD_URL` | ZEO Cloud address offered on the first screen (default `https://app.zeocloud.ae`) |

sections.section: ZEO mobile app (1.25.0) – build it and put it on Google Play › 1. Build the app › B. On a PC with Android Studio
sections.text:
1. Install **Node 22**, **Android Studio** (it brings Java 21 and the Android SDK).
2. In `hrms-project`: `npm ci`, then
   - Windows: `build-android.bat` · Mac / Linux: `./build-android.sh`
   - or step by step: `npm run mobile:build` then `npm run mobile:open` (opens Android Studio → ▶ Run on a phone or emulator).
3. Results: `android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk` and `android/app/build/outputs/bundle/release/app-release.aab`.
4. Signing on the PC: copy `android/keystore.properties.example` to `android/keystore.properties` and fill it in (never share it).

**Every Play Store upload needs a higher version code** (`ZEO_VERSION_CODE`, e.g. 12500 → 12501). Icons and splash come from `resources/` (`npm run mobile:icons` after changing them).

sections.text:
- Go to **play.google.com/console** and create the account with Adept's Google account. One-time registration fee (US$25 when this was written).
- Choose **Organization** (Adept Business Solutions): it needs a **D-U-N-S number** for the company and identity verification of the account owner. Do this first – it can take days.

sections.section: ZEO mobile app (1.25.0) – build it and put it on Google Play › 2. Google Play – first time › 2.2 Create the app
sections.text: Play Console → **Create app**: name **ZEO HR** (or the name Adept chooses), default language English, **App**, **Free**, accept the declarations.

sections.section: ZEO mobile app (1.25.0) – build it and put it on Google Play › 2. Google Play – first time › 2.3 Upload key (once – keep it safe)
sections.text:
Google keeps the real signing key (**Play App Signing**, on by default). Adept signs uploads with an *upload key*:
```
keytool -genkeypair -v -keystore zeo-upload.jks -alias zeo-upload -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000
```
(`keytool` is in Android Studio's `jbr/bin`.) Store `zeo-upload.jks` and its passwords in Adept's password safe. For GitHub: `base64 -w0 zeo-upload.jks` (Mac: `base64 -i zeo-upload.jks`) → secret `ZEO_KEYSTORE_BASE64`. If the upload key is lost, Google can reset it – the app is not lost.

sections.section: ZEO mobile app (1.25.0) – build it and put it on Google Play › 2. Google Play – first time › 2.4 Store listing (Grow → Store presence → Main store listing)
sections.text:
Ready files are in `store/` of the package:

| Item | File / text |
|---|---|
| App icon 512 × 512 | `store/app-icon-512.png` |
| Feature graphic 1024 × 500 | `store/feature-graphic-1024x500.png` |
| Phone screenshots (2–8) | `store/phone-1.png` … `phone-6.png` (1080 × 1920) |
| Short description (80) | *Check in, request leave, see payslips and approve requests – ZEO HR on your phone.* |
| Full description | see 2.7 |
| Category | Business |
| Contact | Adept support e-mail and website |
| Privacy policy | a public page on Adept's website (required: the app uses location and camera) |

sections.section: ZEO mobile app (1.25.0) – build it and put it on Google Play › 2. Google Play – first time › 2.5 App content (Policy → App content) – answer every item
sections.text:
- **Privacy policy** – the URL above.
- **App access** – *All or some functionality is restricted*: give the reviewers a demo server address (https), a login and password of a **demo employee** and of a **demo manager** with approvals waiting, and say that office logins get a code by e-mail (give an ESS login without code to keep it simple).
- **Ads** – No.
- **Content rating** – questionnaire, category *Utility / productivity*; no violence etc. → Everyone.
- **Target audience** – 18 and over.
- **Data safety** – the app collects: *Location – precise* (only at check in / out, for attendance; not shared); *Photos* (selfie with the punch, if the company asks); *Personal info* – name, e-mail, employee code; *Financial info* – salary on payslips; *App info and performance* none; *Device or other IDs* – push token. All sent encrypted (https), not sold, not shared with third parties except Google Firebase for delivering notifications. Data is kept by the employer's ZEO; deletion through the employer (HR).
- **Location permission** – only while the app is open (foreground), so no background-location form is needed.
- **Account deletion** – the app does not create accounts (the employer does); give the support address where an employee can ask for deletion.
- **Government / financial / health apps** – No.

sections.section: ZEO mobile app (1.25.0) – build it and put it on Google Play › 2. Google Play – first time › 2.6 Test, then publish
sections.text:
1. **Testing → Internal testing** → Create release → upload `zeo-1.25.0-release.aab` → release notes → **Save → Review → Start rollout**. Add testers (e-mail list) → they open the opt-in link and install from Play. Internal tests are available within minutes and need no review.
2. Test on several phones: first screen, sign-in (ESS and office with code), fingerprint, check in with GPS / selfie, leave, payslip PDF, approvals, Arabic, notifications.
3. **Production** → Create release → the same (or a newer) .aab → **Countries**: United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait (or all) → **Review → Start rollout**. Google's review usually takes from a few hours to a few days.
4. Updates: raise the version code, build, upload a new release in Production (or test first).

sections.section: ZEO mobile app (1.25.0) – build it and put it on Google Play › 2. Google Play – first time › 2.7 Full description (draft)
sections.text:
> ZEO HR is the mobile app of ZEO, the HR and payroll system for UAE and GCC companies.
> • Check in and out with one tap – with location and a selfie when your company asks for them
> • See your leave balance, request leave and follow its approval
> • Open and share your payslips as PDF
> • Managers approve or reject leave and other requests on the go
> • Fingerprint or face sign-in, notifications for approvals, decisions and payslips
> • English and Arabic
> You need a ZEO login from your employer. The app works with ZEO Cloud and with your company's own ZEO server (version 1.25 or later).

---

sections.section: ZEO mobile app (1.25.0) – build it and put it on Google Play › 3. iPhone (later)
sections.text: `npm i @capacitor/ios@8.5.3 && npx cap add ios` on a Mac with Xcode, an Apple Developer account (yearly fee) and the same steps in App Store Connect. Push on iPhone uses the same Firebase project with an APNs key.

sections.section: ZEO mobile app (1.25.0) – build it and put it on Google Play › 4. Push notifications (Firebase – free)
sections.text:
1. **console.firebase.google.com** → Add project *ZEO* (Analytics not needed).
2. Add app → Android → package **`ae.adept.zeo`** → download **`google-services.json`** → put it in `android/app/` (or the GitHub secret) and build again. Without it the app works, without notifications.
3. Project settings → **Service accounts** → *Generate new private key* → a JSON file. On **every ZEO server** (cloud and customers' own servers) put the file outside the code and set `ZEO_FCM_CREDENTIALS=/path/to/file.json` in `.env`, restart the API. (One Firebase project serves every server; each server only sends to its own users' phones.)
4. Check: sign in on a phone, then *Leave* → request → the manager's phone gets *"Leave to approve"*. The server keeps a log: Django admin → *Push logs*.

sections.section: ZEO mobile app (1.25.0) – build it and put it on Google Play › 5. Good to know
sections.text:
- The app contains the ZEO screens; a newer server keeps working with older apps (mobile API level 1). The server tells old apps to update (`min_app`).
- Company servers on **http** work only for testing (the app warns); use **https** for real data.
- The app sends location **only** with a punch – never in the background.
- `X-ZEO-App` header: every call says the app version and platform (for support).

Follow `INSTALL.md` sections 1–8. The short version (Ubuntu, PostgreSQL, Redis, nginx):

```bash

sections.section: database – the user must own the database (it creates one schema per company)
sections.text:
sudo -u postgres psql -c "CREATE USER zeo_user WITH PASSWORD 'choose-a-strong-password';"
sudo -u postgres psql -c "CREATE DATABASE zeo OWNER zeo_user;"

sections.section: backend
sections.text:
sudo mkdir -p /opt/zeo && sudo chown $USER /opt/zeo
cp -r zeo-hrms /opt/zeo/ && cd /opt/zeo/zeo-hrms
python3 -m venv /opt/zeo/venv
/opt/zeo/venv/bin/pip install --upgrade pip
/opt/zeo/venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env && chmod 600 .env && nano .env      # section 4 of this guide

sections.section: tables, first company, languages
sections.text:

    --admin-email admin@yourcompany.com --branch "Head office" --branch-code HO --uae-leave --expense-defaults \
    --industry OTH --apps hrms,payroll,projects                # asks for the administrator password (10+ characters)
```

Then sign in with the administrator's **e-mail address** and work through **Settings › Setup guide** (15 steps, then Go live).
Leave, attendance, payroll, loans, air tickets and requests – also their imports – are refused until Go live.

sections.section: services, frontend, nginx: INSTALL.md sections 5–7 › 4. The settings file `.env`
sections.text:
Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in at least:

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| `ZEO_SECRET_KEY` | `python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(50))"` |
| `ZEO_DB_NAME`, `ZEO_DB_USER`, `ZEO_DB_PASSWORD`, `ZEO_DB_HOST`, `ZEO_DB_PORT` | the database of section 3 |
| `ZEO_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | the server's host name(s) / IP, comma separated |
| `ZEO_CORS_ORIGINS` | the address users open the app from, e.g. `https://hr.example.com` |
| `ZEO_APP_URL` | the same address – used in e-mail links and password links (**new in the template with 1.67.20**) |
| `ZEO_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` | the same https address; defaults to `ZEO_APP_URL` (**new in the template**) |
| `ZEO_HTTPS` | `true` once the site has a certificate (secure cookies, HSTS); `false` on a plain http test server (**new in the template**) |
| `ZEO_CELERY_BROKER_URL`, `ZEO_REDIS_CACHE_URL` | Redis; `ZEO_CELERY_RESULT_BACKEND` defaults to the broker (**new in the template**) |
| `ZEO_EMAIL_*` | the mail account; empty = e-mails go to the log (testing) |
| `ZEO_DEBUG` | `false` on every server |

The settings themselves already existed in earlier versions; 1.67.20 only lists them in the template. Keep `.env` private
(`chmod 600`) and back it up separately. API keys and passwords live only there – never in the code or the database.

sections.section: services, frontend, nginx: INSTALL.md sections 5–7 › 5. Updating an existing server to 1.79.5 › One-time after the update (if not done with 1.67.19)
sections.text:
```bash
/opt/zeo/venv/bin/python manage.py fix_default_gratuity                         # lists companies whose Gratuity (GTY) is still a payslip addition
/opt/zeo/venv/bin/python manage.py fix_default_gratuity --schema <company> --fix  # per company, after checking with them
```
Gratuity is a provision paid by the final settlement, not monthly cash. Confirm with each company that it does not really pay
gratuity monthly before `--fix`. Payslips already made are not changed.

Check once per company: **Payroll › Employee salary** – formula components that were given to every employee before 1.67.19
are now only for the employees they are assigned to; switch them on where due.

sections.section: services, frontend, nginx: INSTALL.md sections 5–7 › 6. Building the frontend yourself
sections.text:
Only if you change the frontend source; otherwise use `frontend-build/`.

```bash
cd zeo-frontend/hrms-project
npm install
NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 npx ng build --configuration production
```

`ng serve` on a server.

sections.text:
| Symptom | Cause / what to do |
|---|---|
| `DisallowedHost` / "Bad Request (400)" | The host name is missing from `ZEO_ALLOWED_HOSTS` |
| Sign-in works but every screen says "network error" | `assets/env.js` points at the wrong API address, or `ZEO_CORS_ORIGINS` lacks the app address |
| CSRF error on the Django admin over https | `ZEO_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS` / `ZEO_APP_URL` not set to the https address |
| "Finish the setup first" when saving leave or importing | The company's setup guide is not finished – complete it or use **Mark as completed**, then Go live |
| `migrate_schemas` stops with an error | Do not fake migrations. Restore the backup, send the full error output and the version you came from |
| Frontend build "Killed" | Not enough memory – stop the services while building (section 6) |
| Old screens after the update | Users press Ctrl+F5; check that the whole web root was replaced (only `assets/env.js` kept) |

sections.section: ZEO 1.70.2: HSE scope
sections.text:
Version 1.70.2 brings the HSE scope patch (first made as "1.67.27 HSE scope" against 1.67.26) into the full package, on top of 1.70.1. Release notes section 157 has the details and the test results.

The new modules are pages of HSE's generic register screen (list, form, record, actions, PDF, files and record panel). Because of that, the frontend change is small: the menu, the matrix size, and the site fields.

sections.section: ZEO 1.70.2: HSE scope › What is new
sections.text:
| Scope item | Where in ZEO | Rules | |---|---|---| | **12 PPE management** | HSE › PPE, emergency & equipment › PPE issued / PPE catalogue and stock / PPE matrix | The catalogue holds the standard, sizes, life in months, stock and minimum stock.
An issue is refused when stock is short or the size is not offered. Issuing to a blocked contractor worker is also refused.
Replace-by date = issue date + the item's life.
The employee confirms with **I received it**.
A replacement takes stock again. A return goes back to stock only for a reusable item in good condition.
Daily: PPE past its replace-by date changes to **Expired – replace**, and HSE is told about low stock. | | **17 Emergency management** | HSE › … › Emergency plans, Emergency team, Assembly points, Emergency equipment, Emergency drills | Only the HSE manager approves a plan. A fire, evacuation, gas, spill or bomb plan needs an assembly point. Approved plans are open to every employee.
A fire warden or first aider needs a valid competency (FIRE / FA) when the company tracks it.
Equipment (extinguishers, alarms, AEDs, kits …): the next inspection is the last one + the interval. A defect raises a repair action, which needs an owner and a due date. Inspections and services that are overdue are reported daily.
Drills: a drill cannot be recorded in the future. Exceeding the target time, a wrong head count or a weak rating means "improvement needed", and such a drill closes only after an action is raised. | | **18 Equipment safety / certification** | HSE › … › Safety equipment and certificates | Green / yellow / red tags.
A yellow tag needs its restrictions written down. A red tag needs a repair owner and puts the equipment out of service.
An expired certificate turns the tag red (on save

sections.section: ZEO 1.70.2: HSE scope › Deploy
sections.text:
This package is a complete install: copy it as usual (see release notes 157.13). Do **not** run `makemigrations`: ZeoHSE 0006 is in the package.

```
cd zeo-hrms
python manage.py migrate_schemas                  # ZeoHSE 0006 in every company; run it twice
python manage.py load_language_packs
```

1. Restart gunicorn, Celery and beat. The daily HSE job at 07:40 now also checks PPE, emergency equipment, certificates and contractor workers.
2. Users press Ctrl+F5.
3. For existing companies, an HSE manager installs any of the new packs in **Setup › Industry pack**. This only adds content.

sections.section: ZEO 1.70.2: HSE scope › Note from testing – install a new company with nothing else running
sections.text:
On one test install ("freshfm") the API tests were running against the same server while `setup_zeo` worked. That company ended up without the
records for `ZeoMasters 0007_accounting_ready` and `PayrollPlus 0002_rights`. A second install on the same patched code with nothing else running
("recheckfm") had every record and every column. The patch does not touch ZeoMasters or PayrollPlus. Advice: create new companies while no one
is using the server. If a company shows `InconsistentMigrationHistory`, contact support before you run `migrate_schemas` on it.

sections.section: ZEO Developer (ZEO HRMS 1.70.3, built as 1.74.0) – building modules for ZEO HRMS
sections.text:
ZEO offers four levels for adding your own functions. Pick the lowest level that does the job: each higher level needs more skill
and more care when ZEO is updated.

| Level | Who | Where | Survives ZEO updates |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Custom modules | HR / power users | Settings › Custom modules (no code) | yes |
| 2. Formulas, lookups, child tables, links, QR | power users | the same designer, Developer mode on | yes |
| 3. Scripts (Python, API v1) | administrators, consultants | Settings › Developer | yes – API v1 is kept stable |
| 4. Code modules (Django app + Angular page) | developers | your own server / Enterprise | you merge them yourself |

Developer mode is switched on per company: **Settings › Developer mode** (company administrators only). It shows the Developer
menu and the extra field types; switching it off hides them again and stops every script (nothing is deleted).

---

sections.section: ZEO Developer (ZEO HRMS 1.70.3, built as 1.74.0) – building modules for ZEO HRMS › Level 1 – custom modules (existing, ZeoFlow)
sections.text:
A custom module is a list of records with fields, a number (prefix + counter), a Blueprint (states and moves with who may make
them) and rights. Records are stored as JSON in `ZeoFlow.CustomRecord.data`; there is no table per module, so no migration is
ever needed.

sections.section: ZEO Developer (ZEO HRMS 1.70.3, built as 1.74.0) – building modules for ZEO HRMS › Level 2 – calculated fields (new in 1.74.0)
sections.text:
With Developer mode on, the module designer offers six more field types:

| Type | What it holds | Options |
|---|---|---|
| Formula | calculated from other fields | the formula, result: number / money / date / text |
| Lookup | a value from a rate table | `table.column(key_field)`, e.g. `fuel_norm.litres_100km(vehicle_type)` |
| Child table | rows inside the record (max. 500) | columns: `key:Label:type`, types text, number, money, date, choice, yesno, employee |
| Link | a record of another module or app | employee, branch, department, designation, asset, project, `custom:<module>`, `model:<App.model>` |
| QR code / Barcode | an image made from a field or formula | the text formula |

Every field can also have **Show when** and **Required when** (a formula that gives yes / no).

**Formulas** use the payroll formula engine (`PayrollManagement/formula.py`, safe AST evaluation, never `eval`) with the payroll
functions (IF, MAX, MIN, SUM, AVG, ROUND, ABS, INT, FLOOR, CEIL) plus:

```
LOOKUP("rate table", key, "column")      SUMROWS("child", "column")  COUNTROWS("child")  AVGROWS / MAXROWS / MINROWS
TODAY()  DAYS(a, b)  MONTHS(a, b)  YEARS(a, b)  ADDDAYS(d, n)  ADDMONTHS(d, n)  YEAR(d)  MONTH(d)  DAY(d)
CONCAT(a, b, …)  TEXT(v)  UPPER(t)  LEFT(t, n)  BLANK(v)
```

Names are the field keys of the module plus `number` and `state`. Empty dates give 0 (numbers) or empty (dates), so
`IF(BLANK(d), 0, DAYS(d, TODAY()))` works although IF evaluates both branches. The designer refuses unknown names and functions
(with a "did you mean …?"), a field that uses itself, and circles between formulas; formulas are calculated in dependency order.
"Show the formulas on sample records" previews the result on real records before you save.

**Rate tables** (Developer › Rate tables): small table

sections.section: ZEO Developer (ZEO HRMS 1.70.3, built as 1.74.0) – building modules for ZEO HRMS › Level 3 – scripts (new in 1.74.0)
sections.text:
Settings › Developer › Scripts. A script is Python run by ZEO's own interpreter (`ZeoDeveloper/sandbox.py`) – not by Python's
`exec`. Only an allow-list of statements, built-ins and methods exists: no `import`, `class`, `with`, `lambda`, `open`, `eval`,
`getattr`, no names starting with `_`.

sections.section: ZEO Developer (ZEO HRMS 1.70.3, built as 1.74.0) – building modules for ZEO HRMS › Level 3 – scripts (new in 1.74.0) › When a script runs
sections.text:
| Trigger | The script gets |
|---|---|
| Run by hand | nothing (Developer › Scripts › Run) |
| When a record of a module is created / changed / moved | `record` (and `trigger`) |
| Button on the record | `record` – the button shows on the record page |
| Every day / every month (day 1–28, hour) | nothing – Celery beat `zeodeveloper-run-due` runs at minute 10 of each hour |
| When a record of an app is created / changed | `record` = that app's record (any app's record type: CRM lead, work order, HSE incident …) |

sections.section: ZEO Developer (ZEO HRMS 1.70.3, built as 1.74.0) – building modules for ZEO HRMS › Level 3 – scripts (new in 1.74.0) › The script API (v1)
sections.text:
The full reference with an example per function is the **Help** tab. Summary:

```python
records.search("camp_room", {"gender": "Male", "free_beds__gt": 0}, limit=10, order="free_beds")
records.get("vehicle", "VEH-00003");  records.count(...);  records.create("trip", {...})
record["field"], record.rows("fuel"), record.update({...}), record.move("approve", "note")

data.apps(); data.models("crm"); data.fields("ZeoCRM.lead")          # every app
data.search("ZeoProjects.ticket", {"status": "open"}); data.get(key, id); data.count(...)
data.create("ZeoCRM.activity", {...}); data.update(key, id, {...})    # through the app's own screen API

employees.search({...}); employees.get("E0012")                       # read only, scoped by the user's rights

send_email(to, subject, body); notify(who, title, message)
actions.create_task(...); actions.leave_request(...); actions.expense_request(...); actions.document_expiry(...)
actions.payroll_input(...); actions.settlement_deduction(...); actions.post_journal(...)   # wait for approval

today(), now(), add_days, add_months, days_between, month_start, month_end, lookup(table, key, column)
log(...), stop(message), http.get / http.post (allowed sites only), api.version, api.dry_run, api.company
```

sections.section: ZEO Developer (ZEO HRMS 1.70.3, built as 1.74.0) – building modules for ZEO HRMS › Level 3 – scripts (new in 1.74.0) › What keeps scripts safe
sections.text:
* **Same rights as the user.** Every read is scoped like the lists on screen (AccessControl `scope_queryset`, branches, self service
  sees only itself). Every write of another app goes through that app's own API view with the user's login
  (`ZeoDeveloper/internal.py`), including the company guards (read-only / suspended company, licence, HRMS switched off, setup guide
  not finished, an app's setup wizard). A script can never do more than its user could do by hand.
* **Never ZEO's own engine.** Payroll runs, payslips, salary, gratuity, WPS, leave balances, users, rights, login and security
  record types are never written (`appdata.PROTECTED_APPS / PROTECTED_WORDS`). Money goes only through the safe actions.
* **Money waits for an administrator.** `payroll_input`, `settlement_deduction`, `post_journal` and `data.create / update` of a
  record type that holds money (invoices, payments, expenses, journals …) become a *pending* safe action. Another administrator
  approves it in Developer › Actions (the same administrator only when the company has one). Rejecting needs a note.
* **Limits** (Developer › Settings): steps, seconds (5), list / text size, records read (5000) and changed (500) per run, runs per
  month (5000). A script that fails 5 times in a row is switched off and the administrators are told.
* **One run = one transaction.** If the script fails or calls `stop()`, nothing it changed is kept.
* **Test on sample data** runs the script on a chosen record in a transaction that is always rolled back; safe actions and
  `http.post` are only listed. `data.create` gives a planned change (`x.status` "dry", `x.id` None) in a test run.
* **Each company is separate** (one database schema per company). A script cannot reach another company.
* Versions: every saved change

sections.section: ZEO Developer (ZEO HRMS 1.70.3, built as 1.74.0) – building modules for ZEO HRMS › Level 3 – scripts (new in 1.74.0) › Reports, print layouts, scheduled calculations, packages
sections.text:
* **Reports** (Developer › Reports): a list or a summary (group by field / state / month of a date, totals) of a module. They appear
  in the report centre next to ZEO's reports.
* **Print layouts**: HTML with `{{ field }}` and `{% rows child %}…{{ row.column }}…{% endrows %}`; values are escaped; scripts,
  frames, forms, `on…=` and `javascript:` are refused. Opened from the record (Print).
* **Scheduled calculations**: set a field of every record of a module by a formula, monthly or daily (e.g. depreciation).
* **Packages** (Developer › Packages): export modules with their rate tables, scripts, reports, layouts and scheduled calculations
  as one JSON file; import shows a preview (new / change / same) before anything is written.
* **Templates**: two ready apps – *Camp accommodation* (rooms, beds, allocation by gender, occupancy report, allocation letter) and
  *Vehicle log* (vehicles, trips, fuel against the norm, monthly cost, depreciation).

sections.section: ZEO Developer (ZEO HRMS 1.70.3, built as 1.74.0) – building modules for ZEO HRMS › Level 4 – code modules (own server / Enterprise)
sections.text: For what levels 1–3 cannot do (own tables with indexes, heavy calculations, a new integration), write a Django app and an Angular page. `skeleton/` is a working starting point – rename `ZeoAcme` / `acme` everywhere. ``` skeleton/backend/ZeoAcme/ apps.py, models.py, serializers.py, views.py, urls.py, migrations/, tests/ skeleton/backend/ar_terms_acme.json skeleton/frontend/zeo-acme/acme.component.ts ``` Steps: 1. Copy `ZeoAcme` next to `manage.py`; add `'ZeoAcme'` to `TENANT_APPS` in `zeo/settings.py` (every company gets its own tables). 2. `zeo/urls.py`: `path('acme/', include('ZeoAcme.urls'))`. 3. `python manage.py makemigrations ZeoAcme` – **only your app**. Never create migrations in Core, EmpManagement, OrganisationManager, PayrollManagement, ProjectManagement, UserManagement or calendars; link to ZEO's tables with a ForeignKey from your table (as `AcmeRequest.employee`). If makemigrations writes a migration into a ZEO app, delete it. 4. `python manage.py migrate_schemas` (applies to every company). 5. Rights: DRF views are checked by AccessControl automatically (company, `add_ / change_ / delete_ / view_`, branches). Add your own permissions in `Meta.permissions`. 6. Frontend: copy `zeo-acme/` to `src/app/`, add a route under `settings` or `main-sidebar` in `app-routing.module.ts` with `loadComponent`, and a menu item in `shared-ui/menu-config.ts`. Use `ZApi` (adds `?schema=`) for calls. 7. Arabic: put your English → Arabic terms in your own JSON (like `ar_terms_acme.json`) and merge them into `i18n/packs/ar.json` when you build your release; run `python manage.py load_language_packs`. The screens are translated at run time by the English text, so use plain, whole phrases in templates (`Version {{ v }}` rather than mixed t

8. Tests: `tests/test_api.py` (TenantTestCase), or call the API of a test company like the ZeoDeveloper tests (`tests/way3_api.py`).

sections.section: ZEO Developer (ZEO HRMS 1.70.3, built as 1.74.0) – building modules for ZEO HRMS › Files of ZEO Developer
sections.text:
```
zeo-hrms/ZeoDeveloper/            the backend app (TENANT_APPS), migration 0001_v1_74_0_zeo_developer
  sandbox.py    the script interpreter (allow-list, limits)
  api.py        script API v1: records, employees, messages, http, help
  appdata.py    every app: discovery of record types and their screen APIs, reads, writes, app triggers
  internal.py   calls ZEO's API inside the server as the user, through the company guards
  actions.py    safe actions, approvals
  formulas.py   level 2 formulas;  fields.py  the new field types
  services.py   saving, versions, running, limits;  hooks.py  module triggers and buttons
  reports.py    reports, print layouts, QR;  schedule.py / tasks.py  daily and monthly runs
  packages.py   export / import, templates;  templates_apps/*.json  the two demo apps
zeo-frontend/hrms-project/src/app/zeo-developer/   Developer screens, script editor (CodeMirror 6)
```
